=== Page 56 ===
図書館

教育機関における図書館の重要性は改めて述べるまでもないが、武蔵野音楽大学図書館も開館以来、音楽大学図書館としての特殊性と機能を充分に発揮し、本学園ばかりでなく、わが国の音楽教育および学術研究に寄与している。

本館の所蔵する資料は、図書、楽譜、逐次刊行物など図書類とレコード、テープなど視聴覚資料に大別できる。

図書類は楽譜、音楽書、一般図書、逐次刊行物など現在約88,000冊を蔵し、なかでも音楽関係の稀覯図書コレクション（別項参照）は内外に広くその存在が知られている。

LPレコード、SPレコード、テープ、マイクロフィルム、スライドなどの視聴覚資料は現在計約12,000点を保有し、なお年々充実しつつある。

これらの諸資料は本図書館が毎年1回定期的に発行する「年間収書目録」募集状況に応じ逐次刊行する「稀覯図書目録」等により紹介されている。

本図書館は江古田校地、入間校地にそれぞれ独立した機能を備えた施設を誇り、江古田校地図書館には学生閲覧室、参考図書室兼教職員閲覧室、オーディオ研究室、館長室、諸事務室、積層式3層書庫、別置施設としての稀覯図書室、マイクロフィルム撮影室など、また入間校地図書館には閲覧室、特別閲覧室、オーディオ研究室、館長室、整理室、諸事務室など、特に書庫は蔵書数、レコードなどの急増に備え20万部の収蔵可能である。

なお武蔵野高等学校生徒も、大学生と同様この図書館を活用し勉学に励んでいる。

Library

Since the opening of Musashino's library, it has continued to develop to fulfill its function as a musical library not only for the Academia, but for the sake of Japanese musical education as a whole. The library's collection includes books, music scores and periodicals, and also records, tapes, etc. in a separate audio-visual collection. The printed collection includes 88,000 volumes, including a widely-known rare manuscript collection. The audio-visual collection, which presently has approximately 12,000 items, is growing year by year. It encompasses 33-1/3 rpm and 78 rpm records, tapes, microfilms, slides, etc. The library has separate facilities on the Ekoda campus and the Iruma campus.

=== Page 57 ===
Library and Musical Instrument Museum

Reading room

=== Page 58 ===
●稀観図書コレクション●Rare Manuscript Collection

音楽の分野でも最近原典の重要性が認識され、これを基礎とした研究が盛んになってきたが、武蔵野音楽大学図書館ではすでに久しく楽聖達の自筆書簡、自筆楽譜をはじめ古写譜、初版音楽書、楽譜など原典の蒐集に努めており、質量とも優に欧米の音楽図書館に比肩するコレクションを所蔵している。

自筆資料の中でも特に貴重なものは、ベートーヴェンの書簡3通、ラモーの書簡1通、ハイドン、モーツァルト、ウェーバーの寄せ書きなど180点、また自筆楽譜ではバッハの組曲ホ長調、モーツァルトの創作カノン、ハイドンの弦楽4重奏曲“ひばり”、シューベルトの女声4部のための“セレナーデ”のそれぞれ完全に揃ったものなど80点を所蔵している。

これらの資料は堅固な防災施設の稀観図書室に収納されている。

The Musashino Academia Musicae Library collection includes letters and original music scores handwritten by the musical greats, as well as copies of original scores, first editions, etc. In volume and in quality this collection is comparable to those found in the West. The handwritten collection includes such treasures as 3 letters by Beethoven, one by Rameau, and 180 handwritten items by Hayden, Mozart, Weber and others. There are 80 complete original handwritten musical scores, including a handwritten score by Bach for a suite in E-Major, a Mozart “Kanon”, a Hayden string quartet, “The Skylark” and a 4-part serenade for female voice by Schubert.

=== Page 59 ===
●オーディオ研究室●Audio Library

音楽大学および音楽高校では、大規模な視聴覚資料による研究設備を必要とする。
武蔵野音楽大学図書館では江古田校舎に定員50名の、また入間校舎に定員80名の最新機器によるオーディオ研究室を整備している。
このオーディオ研究室はそれぞれ利用者各自がレコード、テープなどの資料を自由に操作取聴するシステムと、保存を要する貴重資料を調整室の係員の操作で取聴するシステムを交錯させて利用の方全を期し、さらにFM2チャンネルを随時受信送出して、教職員、学生生徒の演奏解釈、作曲、音楽学など音楽の全ての分野で、あるいは語学、文学などの研究に大きな成果を挙げている。
現在約12,000点のレコード、テープ、フィルムなどの資料を保有し、これらは性質上細心の注意をもって保管庫に収蔵されている。
利用は整備された体系別目録カードの検索によってなされる。

Musashino Academia Musicae Library has a completely modern audio library on both the Ekoda and Iruma campuses. The former has a seating capacity of 50, the latter, 80. The audio library is open to all to freely use the record and tape systems. The control room staff makes certain that all systems run perfectly. A 2-channel piped-in FM system is available at all times. This system is most effective for various uses by students and teachers in studies of performances, compositions, musicology, and also in language and literature study.
At present, the Audio Library contains about 12,000 records, tapes, microfilms, etc.

●取聴室 Listening room

Musical Instrument Museum
楽器博物館

本学園では20年来音楽文化発展の基盤とすべく世界各
地また各時代の楽器、付属品、音楽に関する装置・器具
類、その他関係資料の蒐集、保存に努めてきた。昭和42
年邦楽器研究家故水野佐平氏からの貴重な邦楽器コレク
ション受贈を契機に、当初の楽器資料室を武蔵野音楽大
学楽器博物館と改称し今日に及んでいるが、現在その所
蔵資料は2,500点に達している。
当博物館の目的は音楽史、楽器学、比較音楽学、また
演奏解釈、古楽器・民族楽器実習など本学園教職員、学
生、生徒の研究と教育に欠くことのできない資料の提供を
第一義としているが、教育機関としての本学園の社会
に対する直接的還元として、許される範囲で学外の方々
へ無料公開をしている。
江古田校地博物館ではこれらの資料を地域的な分類に
より展示し、ヨーロッパの鍵盤楽器、管弦楽器の名器、
弦楽器の名弓コレクションをはじめ世界各国の伝統楽器、
民族楽器を見ることができる。
入間校地博物館には前記水野コレクションを含む邦楽
器、軸管器・蓄音機類、弦楽器工作具類なども併せて約
800点が展示されている。
当館の収蔵品については「収蔵品目録」、各種パンフレ
ット、絵葉書などで紹介されている。

Musashino has assembled over 20 years a collection of musical instruments and accessories that have formed the basis of the development of musical culture. At present, the collection of pieces numbers 2,500.
The primary mission of the museum is to provide the students and teachers with material for research in the study of musical instruments, comparative musicology, studies of performances, antique instruments, folk instruments, etc. However, to the extent possible, the museum also aims at serving the public, and is thus open to all free of charge.
The Ekoda museum's exhibits are arranged according to geographical area. It includes European keyboard instruments, wind and string instruments, a collection of famous instruments, and traditional and folk instruments.
The Iruma campus museum includes the famous Mizuno Collection of Japanese instruments, as well as string, wind and folk instruments, early phonographs, etc., amounting to about 800 items on exhibit.

コンサートホール

●ベートーヴェンホール Beethoven Hall
座席数 1,128。大規模なパイプオルガンを置く本邦初の本格的コンサートホールである。ステージは100名のオーケストラと300名の合唱が同時に演奏できる広さを持ち、学生のオペラ試演のための吊物装置、オーケストラピットも設けられている。
建設計画に先立ち音響設計がなされた数少ないホールの一つで、音響効果の良いホールとして注目を浴び、教授、学生の研究発表、定期演奏会、本学図を訪れる内外一流音楽家による特別演奏、講座などが開催されている。

●モーツアルトホール
座席数500のコンサートホールで、小ホールとしての音響計画がなされ、白を基調にしたインテリアはここで開催される音楽会に気品と風格を与えている。教授、学生の研究発表の他、鑑賞教育、公開講座などに使用される。

Beethoven Hall
Seating 1,128, with a grand pipe organ, this is a full-scale concert hall. The stage can accommodate a 100 piece orchestra and a chorus of 300. There is also a large orchestra pit for student opera performances. Well-known as an acoustically good hall, it is used for student-teacher recitals, regular concerts, and special performances and lectures by outstanding visiting musicians.

Mozart Hall
This concert hall is acoustically designed for an audience of 500. Its white interior motif lends dignity and character to recitals. Besides student and teacher performances, it is also used for music appreciation lessons and public lectures.

=== Page 63 ===
●パイプオルガン
江古田校舎のベートーヴェンホールおよびモーツァルトホールに、それぞれの規模に適したパイプオルガンが設置されている。

ベートーヴェンホールのオルガンは西独ボン市のクライス社製。55ストップで4段の手鍵盤と足鍵盤を有し、各鍵盤に機能的に配置されたパイプ群は総数4,140本のパイプで構成されている。

ストップの配置と整音は18世紀北ドイツのバロック・オルガンを範としているが、それに加えロマン派オルガンのパイプ群、フランス・オルガンの特長を持つリード管群等を取り入れ表現能力を増すよう工夫されており、世界でも大規模な楽器といえる。

モーツァルトホールのオルガンは同クライス社と日本楽器製造株式会社の共同製作になり、14のストップ2段の手鍵盤と足鍵盤947本のパイプを備えているが、特に正面に配置された竹製のパイプ群はこのオルガンに独特の優雅な音色と視覚美を与えている。

上記の他、江古田校舎オルガン研究室、入間校舎オーケストラスタジオおよび古典音楽研究室に、それぞれワルカー社、クライス社、ラウクフ社製のオルガンが設置されている。

Pipe Organs
The concert halls on Ekoda campus contain two pipe organs, one in Beethoven Hall and one in Mozart Hall, on different respective scales. The Beethoven Hall organ was built by the Klais Company in Bonn. With 55 stops and 4-tiered hand and foot keyboards, it has 4,140 pipes.

The Mozart Hall organ was jointly manufactured by Klais and by the Japan Musical Instrument Manufacturing Corporation. It has 14 stops, 2-tiered hand and foot keyboards and 947 pipes. It features a set of bamboo pipes in the front that impart an elegance to the organ's tones. Besides the above organs, the Ekoda campus also has an organ study hall. On the Iruma campus, the Orchestra, Studio and Classical Music Study Halls each have organs made by Walker, Klais and Laukhuff respectively.

●モーツァルトホール Mozart Hall

Thoughts on the Coming 50th Anniversary of the Founding of Musashino Academia Musicae

バルトーク像
（ハンガリー共和国より寄贈）
Béla Bartók
(Gift of the Hungarian People's Republic)

=== Page 68 ===
学校法人武蔵野音楽学園では、従前から優秀な指導者によって豊かな人間性に基づく充実した教育と、理想的な音楽教育環境の具現を強く主張していたが、すでに久しく江古田校地の学園キャンパスとしての狭隘と都市公害から受ける制約を憂慮して、東京の西郊入間市の45万㎡におよぶ広大な入間校地に、その風光を充分に生かし、教室棟、研究室棟、練習室棟などの校舎群、体育館、総合グランド、テニスコートなどの運動施設、図書館、研修所、男子学寮、女子学寮、エネルギーセンター、レストラン棟などの附属施設を逐次完成、現在その建設工事の総決算とも言える大講堂を建設中であり、この時代を先取した学園環境は改米にまで広く知られるようになった。

音楽における一貫教育、早期教育の重視は改めて述べるまでもなく内外の音楽教育界の趨勢であるが、本学園ではこれら音楽教育界の動向、音楽芸術の研鑽と相俟って人間形成を指向する教育方針、またこれまでの優れた環境研究の成果を基礎として、この校地に大学音楽学部の一部を移転、さらに武蔵野高等学校音楽科を、また本学園既設の3幼稚園に加えて武蔵野幼稚園を設置している。

本学園では、昭和54年に迎える学園創立50周年を向後発展への契機ととらえて、この自然と人間との関わりと、"和"のこころを尊重した環境の中ではじめて可能といっても過言ではない、創造力漲る音楽芸術の研鑽と人間形成を目指した教育を一層強力に推し進める覚悟であり、優れた教授陣のもとに江古田、入間両校地の融合を計ることによって、日々発展する社会の要請に即応できる教育体制を確立して、国際的な立場から音楽文化向上の一端を担う本学園に寄せられる内外の期待に応える所存である。

Thoughts on the Coming 50th Anniversary of the Founding of the Musashino Academia Musicae
学園創立50周年に臨んで

At the fully accredited Musashino Academia Musicae, students receive a solid education based on the high ideals of character building under the guidance of highly qualified teachers. This environment was realized as a result of a long-held concern to free students from the dirty and crowded conditions of the city. An extensive hillside area encompassing 450,000 m² was provided accordingly, to create Iruma Campus. Since then, the gymnasium, athletic grounds, library, seminar houses, dormitories, Energy Center, etc. have each been built in their turn. Finally, to complete the work, a large auditorium is now under construction.

As Musashino looks forward to its 50th anniversary in 1979, we may well consider that we have reached a turning point in our further development. This environment is the first of its kind in Japan, where the relationship between man and nature and the spirit of mutual friendship are emphasized in the encouragement of creative musical artistry and character development. With the aid of the Ekoda and Iruma campuses and our superior teaching staff, an educational system that fulfills the requirements of society has become possible. From the international standpoint as well, Musashino is looked to as a bearer of culture for all.

=== Page 69 ===
新講堂計画● Outline of Projected New Auditorium

大岡校地正門附近の小高い北東斜面に建設中の新講堂は、座席数1200、移動椅子200の、音響効果を充分配慮したワンフロアの大講堂である。正面には大規模なパイプオルガンを設置し、ステージは大編成のオーケストラと合唱が同時に演奏出来る充分な広さをもち、電動昇降式オーケストラピットや学生のオペラ試演のための吊物装置等も設けられている。ステージにふらなるサイドステージ及び準備室、小教室3室、出演者控室、スタッフ指令室をはじめ、放送室、照明室、映写室、医務室、その他管理事務室、空調機械室等が設けられており、全館冷暖房で調光式照明が設備され、エレベーターも用意されている。1、2、3階の各ロビーからは、自然に恵まれた武蔵野のそれぞれの景観が一望される。大講義、講演、また職員、学生及び外来音楽家による演奏研究等に活用され、さらにそのあい間に落ち着いて談話のできる憩の場も設けられている。

〈表紙〉
J.J.ベルモント作
"Ch.F.グノー：「ファウスト」のバレエ音楽からの印象"(部分)
本学園は昭和52年、米国の高名な画家J.J.Belmont氏（1877－1964）が残した名作8点を同氏ご本人から寄贈された。
ベルモント氏は当時活躍した多くの音楽家と親交が厚く、音楽と絵画の二大芸術の融合——音楽から受ける印象や雰囲気をスペクトルの7色に対応させて表現しようとする——を目指して、「カラーミュージック」(Color-Music Paintings)という油絵の新しいジャンルを開いた印象派の流れを踏む画家である。
同氏の作品はハーファル美術館、ブレスト美術館、東京近代美術館、ジュリアード音楽院などに収蔵されており、それぞれに表題としてインスピレーションを得た曲名と、そのメロディーの一部（楽譜）が付されている。
本学園所蔵の作品は、入間校地楽器博物館内に展示されている。

（表紙）
J.J.ベルモント作
“Ch.F.ダーノ：「ファウスト」の
バレエ音楽からの印象”（部分）
本学園は昭和52年、米国の高名な画家J.J.Belmont氏（1877－1964）が残した名作8点を同氏亡き後から寄贈された。
ベルモント氏は当時活躍した多くの音楽家と親交が厚く、音楽と絵画の二大芸術の融合——音楽から受ける印象や香気をスペクトルの7色に対応させて表現しようとする——を目指して、「カラー音楽」（Color-Music Paintings）という油絵の新しいジャンルを開いた印象派の流れを踏む画家である。
同氏の作品はルーブル美術館、ブカレスト美術館、東京近代美術館、ジュリアード音楽院などに蔵されており、それぞれに表題としてインスピレーションを得た曲名と、そのメロディーの一部（楽譜）が付されている。
本学園所蔵の作品は、入間校地楽器博物館内に展示されている。

What is the Asian Youth Music Camp?

The establishment of a regional Asian Youth Music Camp Association to serve as the basis of an on-going project for the development, interaction and co-existence of young people from the Austral-Asian region was an idea and the vision of Mr. Maslyn Williams, an Australian writer, who was very much involved with the music camp movement in Australia.

In April, 1976, while attending the inauguration of the National Arts Centre of the Philippines, Mr. Williams made a proposal to Madame Imelda Romualdez Marcos, First Lady of the Philippines, and to experts from various countries invited to the inauguration that youthful talents from the Asian region should be convened into a music camp in the Philippines. This proposal was enthusiastically received and the Inaugural Asian Youth Music Camp was held at Mount Makiling of the Philippines from 1st to 15th of May, 1977. To the first camp, Hong Kong sent five young musicians and one official.

Following the success in the Philippines, the 2nd Asian Youth Music Camp was held in Singapore in December 1978 and Hong Kong was represented by twelve young musicians and two officials. It was at this Camp that Hong Kong was invited to be host country of the 1979 Camp.

The 1979 Asian Youth Music Camp will be held at the Wu Kwai Sha Youth Village, Hong Kong, from 1st to 15th December. Over a hundred participants from Indonesia, Japan, Korea, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Macau and Australia will come and join the best young players from Hong Kong to take part in the two-week residential music camp. At the Camp the 1979 Asian Youth Orchestra will be formed and the Orchestra will give four public concerts for Hong Kong audience. The young musicians will study under instructors coming from the Austral-Asian region as well as famous musicians from the United Kingdom and the United States of America.

The main goals of the music camp are music making and exchange of experiences among young people from different countries. Life in the music camp will be fun, pleasure as well as hard work.

At the Hong Kong Camp, two new targets have been set. First, work on the Constitution of the Asian Youth Music Camp Association, started in the Philippines and in Singapore, will be finalised by the representatives of the countries attending the Camp. Second, in addition to rehearsing classical and contemporary western music, the playing of ethnic music on ethnic instruments will be encouraged. In Hong Kong, the term "ethnic" refers to Chinese music and traditional Chinese instruments. It is therefore Hong Kong's pleasure to invite to the Camp the Singapore Youth Chinese Orchestra which will join the Hong Kong Youth Chinese Orchestra and eighteen other Hong Kong Chinese orchestras, choirs and dance groups in the rehearsal and performance of Chinese instrumental music, songs and dances.

亚洲青年音乐营是什么？

亚洲青年音乐营始创人是澳洲作家威廉士先生。威廉士对青年音乐活动非常热心，为澳洲国立音乐营协会委员。

一九七六年四月，威廉士先生应邀参加菲律宾国立艺术中心开幕典礼。他向菲律宾第一夫人艾美黛及其他应邀参加该次典礼的音乐及文化界先进提出举办亚洲音乐营的建议，得到各国代表热烈支持。

第一届亚洲青年音乐营随即于一九七七年五月在菲律宾的MOUNT MAKILING 成功举行。香港亦有五名青年乐手及一工作人员代表参加。亚洲青年音乐营目的在给予亚洲各国及澳洲的青年乐手一个交流音乐知识和互相切磋的机会，同时促进亚洲的青年音乐活动及使澳洲和亚洲人民能更紧密合作。

第二届亚洲青年音乐营于一九七八年十二月在新加坡举行。香港派出十二名青年乐手及两名工作人员代表参加。

本届亚洲青年音乐营由香港主办，于本年十二月一日至十五日在中华基督教青年会乌溪沙青年新村举行。将有十地国家（印尼、日本、韩国、马来西亚、菲律宾、新加坡、泰国、澳门、澳洲及香港）百馀名代表参加。

来自上述各国的青年乐手将与香港的杰出青年音乐新秀在营中共度两星期，在澳洲及亚洲各国，英国及美国的著名音乐家指导下练习，组成一九七九年亚洲青年管弦乐团，为本港观众作四场公开表演，营中生活工作与娱乐并重，将为参加者带来一个宝贵的音乐学习切磋机会。

本届音乐营活动，将包括两项创举，其一是亚洲青年音乐营协会的会章，将会在营中议定，以使音乐营活动的延续，更趋稳健。其二是除练习西洋音乐作品外，本届音乐营将加演亚洲音乐家的民族音乐作品。为此特别邀请新加坡青年华乐团及十九队本港中乐团（包括香港青年中乐团），合唱团及舞蹈团参加演出中乐作品多首，使音乐营更具地方色彩。

=== Page 4 ===
I would like to welcome the young musicians and their leaders from Asia, Australia and New Zealand to the Third Asian Youth Music Camp. Hong Kong is honoured to host the camp and I am sure your music will bring as much happiness to yourselves as to your audiences in this city.

Music is an ideal link between people of different background and culture. The spirit of brotherhood created at this camp will, I am sure, give the participants a better understanding of the people and countries of Australasia. This understanding is important not only for the young musicians' future careers but in helping to bring about a peaceful and harmonious world community.

I wish all participants a successful and enjoyable Camp.

( Jack Cater )
Acting Governor

A new generation of performers and audiences for Hong Kong

The Music Administrator's Office was established in October, 1977 with three objectives: to run an instrumental music training programme; to promote interest in music, especially among the young; and to encourage and assist in the organising of music activities at all districts. In gist, the Office is preparing the audience and the performers for the 1980s, the 1990s and the 21st century

The Office now runs nine youth orchestras: two youth symphony orchestras, three youth symphonic bands and four youth Chinese orchestras. In addition, 2,500 students are taking weekly lessons, playing different Chinese and Western instruments. Courses for aural training, theory and music appreciation are also run at the four music centres of the Office. Next year, the number of trainees will be doubled. By then there will be training classes in every district of the territory. For talented young musicians, special training is provided at both local and overseas training centres. The Office also offers scholarship for advanced students.

Besides instrumental music training, the Office has organised six choirs in Sham Shui Po, Sai Kung, Kwai Chung, Mong Kok, Sha Tin and Chai Wan. More children and youth choirs will be organised in the coming months.

Music for the Millions

Another major activity of the Office is the "Music for the Millions" concert programme. The purpose of this programme is to introduce music to new audiences.

A total of 587 "Music for the Millions" concerts have so far been organised for 377,500 people. These concerts are given by youth orchestras, bands and ensembles and they are held in schools, parks, playgrounds, community halls and factories.

To broaden the outlook and experience of young musicians in Hong Kong, overseas musicians passing through Hong Kong are invited to run master classes and seminars. Up to mid-November, 1979 a total of 92 master classes and seminars have been held for over 3,600 students and music lovers. Musicians who have taken part as tutors in master classes include Eudice Shapiro, CHIU Sin-tung, Jonathan Williams, Christian Ferras, LIM Kek-beng, Bela Siki, FOU T'song, Susan Starr, Richard Markson and many others.

International music exchange programmes

The Office also organises international music exchange programmes. The County of Avon Schools Orchestra from the United Kingdom visited Hong Kong at the end of July, 1978. Four public concerts were given for an audience of over 11,000. The Hong Kong Youth Symphony Orchestra and Youth Chinese Orchestra paid a return visit to Avon in August, 1979.

In November, 1978 the Nakamura Gakuen Girls High School Band from Japan was invited to be the guest band at the First Hong Kong Youth Symphonic Band Festival jointly organised by the Music Administrator's Office and the Tom Lee Music Foundation.

Three joint performances with 12 local bands were given for an audience of over 15,000 people. In May, 1979 the Philippines Youth Orchestra visited Hong Kong. Two public concerts were given for an audience of 2,700 people. In June, the Australian Youth Orchestra came to Hong Kong and gave one performance for an audience of 1,300 people.

The Second Hong Kong Youth Symphonic Band Festival was held in November, 1979. Two guest bands came: one from Singapore and the other from the Philippines. They joined 23 Hong Kong bands and gave 5 public concerts for an audience of 18,000.

=== Page 7 ===
「樂韻播萬千」

「樂韻播萬千」音樂會是統籌處另一項重要活動，主要目的是向觀眾介紹音樂。統籌處安排不同中西樂隊到各區的學校、公園、遊樂場、社區會堂及工廠演奏。迄今，共舉辦了五百八十七個「樂韻播萬千」音樂會，供有377,500名觀眾欣賞。

為使本港青年音樂家有機會增進見識和經驗，統籌處經常邀請訪港各國音樂家主持指導班和研討會。至今年十一月中，統籌處已為本港三千六百餘名青年樂手安排了九十二個指導班及研討會。受邀請的音樂家包括沙比露、趙善同、威廉士、花利士、林克明、絲琪、傅聰、蘇珊絲特雅、馬克愷及其他著名音樂家。

國際青年音樂交流

為推廣國際青年音樂交流及使本港青年有機會欣賞外國青年樂手的演奏，統籌處安排連串的音樂交流活動。去年七月，雅幌郡青年管樂團由英國專程來港，與本港青年樂團及合唱團合奏四場音樂會，聽衆人數達一萬一千人。香港青年交響樂團及青年中樂團於本年八月赴英演出，亦曾回訪雅幌郡。

去年十一月，一隊日本著名女子管樂團，應邀參加由統籌處及通利音樂基金聯合主辦之「第一屆香港青年管樂節」，並與本港十二隊管樂團聯合演出三場音樂會，聽衆人數達一萬五千人。本年五月，菲律賓青年交響樂團應邀到港，與香港青年交響樂團及青年管樂團聯合演出兩場，聽衆人數達二千七百名。在六月，澳洲青年交響樂團到港演出，聽衆達一千三百名。

本年十一月，二隊管樂隊從新加坡及菲律賓來港參加「第二屆香港青年管樂節」，與二十三隊本港管樂團聯合演出五場音樂會，觀衆達一萬八千人。

香港新一代的演奏者及觀眾

音樂事務統籌處於一九七七年十月成立，宗旨有三：安排全港性器樂訓練計劃，提高社會人士（特別是青年人）對音樂的興趣及鼓勵和協助各區舉辦音樂活動。總括來說，統籌處旨在培植新一代的演奏者及觀眾。

統籌處現已成立九個樂團，包括兩個青年交響樂團、三個青年管樂團及四個青年中樂團。另外開設中西器樂訓練班，訓練二千五百名中小學生。視聽訓練、音樂理論及音樂欣賞會等各類活動，亦經常在四個訓練中心舉行。明年，訓練總人數將倍增至五千名，到時全港九新界都會有器樂訓練班。對賦天才的青年音樂家，統籌處在香港或海外多處為他們安排適當的訓練，並設有獎學金。

除器樂訓練外，統籌處並積極推行合唱團訓練。現時已有六個合唱團，分別在深水埗、西貢、葵涌、旺角、沙田及柴灣成立。統籌處更計劃在未來數月間成立多個兒童及青少年合唱團。

=== Page 8 ===
The Urban Council: Cultural Programmes and Facilities

fundamental task of the Urban Council is the provision of programmes that enrich the cultural life of Hong Kong.

The Council directly sponsors two major arts festivals annually: The Festival of Asian Arts, the International Film Festival and makes financial contribution to the annual Hong Kong Arts Festival. In addition, the Council has established the professional Chinese Orchestra and Repertory Theatre. It also operates the Hong Kong Museum of Arts, the Hong Kong Museum of History, and will soon open the Hong Kong Space Museum.

Directly and indirectly the Council supports local talent and brings overseas artists to local audiences in a programme of performances at over 80 indoor and outdoor locations, including parks and playgrounds, schools, libraries, and civic association halls in every district of Hong Kong. Finally it fully or partially sponsors over 600 performance events at three City Hall stages annually.

CITY HALL

The City Hall is the major cultural centre of Hong Kong. It is in fact a complex that houses three performance venues (a concert hall, a theatre and a recital hall), the Hong Kong Museum of Arts, two public exhibition galleries and the cultural public library. During the year 1978-79 over 300,000 people attended 685 Urban Council presentations of concerts, puppet shows, recitals, operas, films, dramas, lectures and dance at the Concert Hall, Theatre and Recital Hall.

Among the many internationally renowned artists who appeared under the auspices of the Urban Council in 1978-79 were pianists Fou T'song, Gyorg Sandor, Nancy Loo; cellists Pierre Fournier, Martin Sieghart, Jonathan Williams; violinists Theo Olof, Jack Glatzer, Christian Ferras; guitarists Julian Byzantine, Alice Artzt; the Stuttgart Ballet, The Dublin Festival Theatre, the Cleveland Orchestra, the Israel Philharmonic Orchestra, the Mozarteum Orchestra of Salzburg and NDR Orchestra of Hamburg.

Besides regular monthly performances by its own Chinese Orchestra and Repertory Theatre, the Council helps to underwrite a regular performance schedule by the Hong Kong Philharmonic Orchestra. It also co-sponsors periodic chamber music and solo recitals by guest musicians playing with either of the two orchestras, or by section leaders and individual musicians from their ranks performing separately.

OUTDOOR VENUES

Apart from bringing as much local, regional and international talent to Hong Kong stages as is possible, the Council cultural goals include assuring every district of Hong Kong a stage of its own and entertainments with which to fill it — usually free.

There are over 80 performance sites throughout Hong Kong now in use. But the best index of Council district activities is recorded in its free outdoor performance programmes. In what must be one of the world's more ambitious efforts, 827 individual performances and fetes were offered in the year 1978/79. These were attended by over 800,000 people and included variety shows, Chinese operas, puppet theatre, pop concerts, fun fairs, children's parties, youth dances, and film presentations.

CULTURAL COMPLEX

Tsim Sha Tsui Cultural Complex, near the Star Ferry Wharf in Kowloon, is a new multi-purpose structure scheduled for completion in the early 1980s. The Complex will include a 2300-seat Concert Hall, a 2200-seat Lyric Theatre and a 500-seat Studio Theatre which, with present City Hall venues, will almost triple the existing seating capacity for performances in Hong Kong. The new centre will also house the Space Museum, and the Museum of Arts will be relocated to separate buildings on the premises. Once completed, the new facility will make Hong Kong's physical facilities for housing cultural events in par with any in Asia.

=== Page 9 ===
基本服務

市政局的基本服務之一，是提供各類文娛節目，以充實市民的文化生活。

市政局每年主辦兩個規模龐大的藝術節：亞洲藝術節及國際電影節。又贊助每年一度的香港藝術節。此外，市政局並創辦了職業化的香港中樂團及香港話劇團，而香港藝術館，香港博物館及即將落成啓用的太空館，都是市政局轄下的機構。

市政局主辦或聯合贊助本港俊彥及海外藝術家在八十多處戶內或戶外地方演出，包括公園、遊樂場、學校、圖書館及各社區會堂等。每年在大會堂演出的節目達六百多項。

大會堂是本港文藝薈萃的中心，內設有三處表演文娛節目的場地（音樂廳、劇院和演奏廳）、香港藝術館，兩所展覽廳及公立圖書館。

一九七八至七九年度，即有三十多萬的觀衆到大會堂欣賞市政局所主辦的各類節目，包括音樂會、木偶戲、獨奏會、歌劇、電影、戲劇、講座及舞蹈等，凡六百八十五項之多。

一九七八至七九年度，由市政局邀請來港演出的國際知名藝術家計有：鋼琴家傅聰、喬治·桑達·羅乃新、大提琴家彼埃·湯尼爾、馬田·薛夏德、莊納丹、威廉斯；小提琴家菲奧·柯度夫、積基薩、基士丁、賈拉斯；結他手朱利安·畢先達、愛麗·雅芝，此外，尚有史圖加芭蕾舞蹈團、都柏林劇團、克里夫蘭管弦樂團、以色列管弦樂團、莎爾茲堡莫扎特管弦樂團及漢堡NDR交響樂團。各國領事館及文化團體亦有參與其事，協辦部份藝術家來港獻藝。

市政局轄下的香港中樂團及話劇團每月均作定期演出。此外，市政局亦贊助香港管弦樂團的定期演出，並經常舉辦室樂演奏會及獨奏會，由應邀來港的音樂家與兩大樂團之一演奏，或由樂團音部的首席樂手與團員分別演奏。

戶外文娛節目

市政局除儘量贊助本港、亞洲及國際藝壇精英在港演出外，並致力普及文藝，務使本港每一區域均有提供文娛活動的場所，而表演通常是免費的。

目前可作爲戶外演出的場地達八十多處，一九七八至七九年度內演出的戶外節目達八百二十七項，規模之大較諸世界任何一國，不遑多讓，觀衆者逾八萬人。節目多姿多采，包括綜合性節目、粵劇、木偶戲、流行音樂會、遊藝會、兒童聯歡會、青年舞會及電影欣賞等。去年的亞洲藝術節，市民不但踴躍購票參觀（平均銷票，達百分之九十八），並有七萬五千多人，欣賞二十六項在戶外場地演出的免費節目，各外來藝術團體均有參加演出。

文娛館

尖沙咀文娛館位於九龍火車站舊址，是一所設備完善能作多種用途的文娛中心，擬在一九八○年代落成。文娛館設有一個二千三百座位的音樂廳，一個二千二百座位的歌劇院和一個五百座位的小型劇場。這樣一來連同現有大會堂計算在內，座位數量將比現時增多三倍。文娛館裏亦建有太空館，而香港藝術館亦會遷移到該處，文娛館全部落成啓用後，香港的文娛設備足以與亞洲任何文化中心媲美。

"Great music harmonizes with the Universe"—this is a common belief of Chinese philosophers. Music is the best communication medium among the races.

During the coming two weeks, all the young musicians from the Austral-Asian region will work and study together; this will not only improve the musicianship of each participant but also help to develop mutual understanding and friendship. With the development of this type of activities, we can foresee a brightful future in the music world of Austral-Asia.

During the music camp, various compositions from all over the world will be performed. In particular, some of the best compositions by Asian composers will also be played. On this point, the Asian Youth Music Camp is sharing the same goal with the Asian Composers' League, and this is something we are pleased and proud of.

Therefore, on behalf of the Asian Composers' League, I wish to send the best wishes and most sincere congratulations to all the participants and organisers of the 1979 Asian Youth Music Camp.

=== Page 13 ===
OVERTURE IN D MINOR
George Frederic Handel (1685-1759)
(arranged by Edward Elgar)

In 1718, Handel joined the crowd of artists and intellectuals working at Cannons, the magnificent estate of James Brydges, Duke of Chandos. A visitor recorded that "the Chapel (of Cannons) hath... a Choir of Vocal and Instrumental Musick, and when his Grace goes to Church, he is attended by his Swiss Guards; his Musick also play when he is at Table." And some of that princely music was by Handel himself, including eleven anthems known now as the Chandos Anthems. The second, "In the Lord Put I My Trust", uses a text drawn from Psalms 9, 11, 12 and 13.

The stately Overture which opens the anthem attracted the attention of Edward Elgar, composer-in-residence to Victorian England. Caught by the nobility-and grandeur of Handel's music in general (echoes of the oratorios and operas abound in Elgar's works; "Dove son" and "Pomp and Circumstance" have much in common), and of this overture in particular, Elgar used his prodigious orchestral talents to clothe the Baroque original in a symptuous, sonorous evening dress.

TAI PING SHAN PANORAMA
Doming Lam (Born 1935)

Born in Macau, Doming Lam had his conservatory training in Toronto, going on the advanced work at the University of Southern California. Since returning to Hong Kong in 1964, he has been one of the city's most active composers and promoters of new music; his "Thanksgiving to Joe-Kwan", commissioned by RTHK, was selected for the 1979 International Rostrum of Composers, held in Paris in May this year.

One of Lam's preoccupations has been the integration of Chinese and Western musical procedures; his works are dramatic and colourful, displaying an extraordinary keeness of orchestration. "Tai Ping Shan Panorama" was written especially for the Music Administrator's Office in Hong Kong.

FANTASIA
Young Jin Kim (Born 1930)

Kim, born in Taejon, Korea, attended Seoul National University where he obtained his Bachelor's and Master's Degrees in music. He then went to the U.S. for four years of advanced work, in New York and Illinois. He is currently an associate professor at Seoul National University.

Among his major works are a Brahmatic Ode, (for 4 groups of strings and percussion); and "Yo Eum", for orchestra. Kim's works are complex in construction, though, like many Korean composers, he occasionally utilizes sounds in a purely sensual way recalling the Western avant-garde.

SUN MUSIC III
Peter Sculthorpe (Born 1929)

Born 50 years ago, Sculthorpe studied at the University of Melbourne and Oxford; among his teachers were Edmund Rubbra and Egon Wellesz. Since 1963, he has taught at the University of Sydney.

Sculthorpe is one of the most arresting voices from a country which has only recently emerged as a major musical power. He himself claims little interest in European music, preferring to concentrate on Australian material. He also believes that Asian music principles can revitalize the creative world of the West. "Sun Music" demonstrates this in several ways, notably in its basic principles. Sculthorpe has tried to create a piece of music whose main structural element is pure sound, in a sensual way, rather than themes and developments in a traditional Western, post-Beethoven manner. To achieve this he provides, as he himself says,

A new repertory of instrumental resources — microtonal and semi-tonal clusters on strings and brass, slow string glissandi, slowly shifting brass chords of changing accents and dynamics, a dense shimmering string chord of 59 adjacent quarter-tones... to create music of a static, incantatory, almost frighteningly inhuman kind. It is a music of harsh colours, of a brilliant light which glistens and blazes, music which perhaps could only come out of a country in which heat — not cold — is the enemy element.

"Sun Music" is scored for an orchestra of modest size, but with a vastly expanded percussion division, which includes traditional instruments but also a variety of Asian and exotic sound-sources as well.

"ESPAÑA" RHAPSODY
Emmanuel Chabrier (1841-1894)

Originally trained as a law clerk, Chabrier spent 18 long years at the Ministry of the Interior in Paris. In his spare time, however, he moved among artists and musicians such as Claude Manet, Renoir, Verlaine, and Faure. When he was 40, he visited Bayreuth, and the operas of Wagner made such an impression on him that he resolved to leave his job and commit himself to the life of a professional composer. He was only to live 13 years longer, but in that brief time he created a body of distinctly original and striking music.

His first "professional" works were piano pieces — natural enough, as he was nearly of virtuoso standard himself. But a visit to Spain stimulated his imagination (as hundreds of witty letters from him to his friends testify) and he summed up his recollections in this Rhapsody.

=== Page 14 ===
It is based on actual Spanish dance themes, from Seville, Granada, and the Alhambra. One of the most attention-getting, though — the jolly trombone theme which appears at the end — is pure Chabrier.

PHILIPPINE SCENES
Lucrecia Kasilag
One of the most active and admired figures of music in the Philippines, Lucrecia Kasilag is president of the Cultural Center of the Philippines and works with numerous government and professional bodies associated with music and the arts. Trained in the Philippines and at the Eastman School of Music, she has written more than 200 compositions, ranging from folk-song settings and art songs to choral, chamber and orchestral works.

Lucrecia Kasilag has long pioneered in the research of, and utilisation of, Asian musical instruments side-by-side with orthodox Western instruments, resulting in numerous compositions with an East-West blend.

"Philippine Scenes", composed in 1974, quotes themes from three separate regions of the Philippines — Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao. The first movement, "Mountainside," is rhapsodic and pastoral in character, building upon a plaintive flute solo. The following "Lullaby" is a quiet, languid song, while the final "Festival!" is a picture of a village celebration, a fiesta of folk rhythms, native instruments and shouting by the musicians (both those in the village and those on-stage!)

DANCE OF THE DOLL
Law Wing-Fai (Born 1949)
Born in Hong Kong, Law Wing-Fai studied composition with Hsu Tsang-Houei at the Taiwan National University. On his return to Hong Kong, he worked in music education for several years, and served as tutor in classical guitar at the Chinese University. In 1977, he went to America, working with John Crowford at the University of California, which awarded him a Master's Degree in Music for his work in composition.

Hong Kong first became aware of Law Wing-Fai's talents with his composition for pi-pa, "Silkworm", written in 1972. The work was a strikingly original combination of traditional and innovative techniques, organized in a system of free tonality. Another of his works, "Mulberry Grove Dance," for flute and guitar, was selected to be sent to the International Rostrum of Composers, held under the auspices of the International Music Council in Paris earlier this year.

His most recent compositions, such as "Seu-Chu-Kou" (1978) and the "String Quartet" (1978), as well as the orchestral piece "Chien" (1978), are attempts to use atonal techniques in the service of Chinese aesthetics. "Dance of the Doll" was written especially for the Music Administrators Office in Hong Kong.

DOUBLE-BASS CONCERTO IN A MINOR
Domenico Dragonetti
The "Paganini of the double-bass," Dragonetti was born in Venice, where, while still in his teens, he joined the musical establishment at St. Mark's Cathedral. He was a prodigious composer as well as performer, turning out sonatas, concertos and capriccios by the dozen. His reputation spread outside of Italy, and he eventually accepted a post in London, where he died. During his travels across Europe, he came to know and befriend many of the great composers of the day; he and Haydn were close friends, and he knew Beethoven well also.

His personal life was a colourful one; he kept, for example, a huge collection of dolls, some of which accompanied him to concerts. His dog Carlo also went along, and would sit beside him in the orchestra pit. His collection of snuff-boxes was also remarkable, filling an entire gallery.

Dragonetti left hundreds of compositions for double-bass, many of them still in manuscript in the British Museum. There is, for example, a curious arrangement of the pedal parts for Bach's organ fugues. Tonight's concerto, on the other hand, is a more traditional work, frequently performed — whenever a bass-player of sufficiently accurate agility can be found to undertake it!

CONCERTO FOR DOUBLE STRING ORCHESTRA
Michael Tippett (Born 1905)
Acknowledged as one of Britain's most intelligent and individual musicians, Tippett is a slow and meticulous writer whose output is dwarfed beside that of composers such as Britten. Still there are several large works — three operas and an oratorio — as well as three symphonies and a handful of orchestral, choral and chamber works.

Tippett was born in London, but spent most of his life in the country. A confirmed pacifist, he spent three months in jail for his beliefs when war broke out in the 1930's. Later, he was appointed Music Director at Morley College, succeeding Gustav Holst. There Tippett organized concerts which became famous throughout London for their quality and diversity.

At the same time he completed tonight's Concerto, one of his best-known works. It calls for two groups of string players, giving the composer opportunities for rhythmic and echo effects between the two. The warm tone of the strings seems to have stimulated Tippett's lyrical creativity, especially in the third movement finale. There, amid much rhythmic complexity, a luscious tune resembling a Negro spiritual wells up in the bass, leading the entire work to a powerful conclusion.

OVERTURE "1812"
Peter I. Tchaikovsky
Tchaikovsky is in the odd position of being appreciated too much and too little — too much, perhaps, by the musical novice, who finds in him even greater satisfaction than in Beethoven; too little, perhaps, by the trained musical analysts, who may magnify his faults until they overshadow his genius. The truth is probably somewhere in between the two, with leanings towards the novice's side; there are moments in his music which it would be impossible to find elsewhere, pages in which he expresses elemental passions with a simple directness that all can appreciate. His music, personal and powerful, has been an emotional experience for masses of music-lovers because he knew how to speak simply and honestly. Millions

=== Page 15 ===
have been touched by the pessimism of the final symphonies, the yearnings of Romeo and Juliet, the sweetness of the A minor trio, the enchantment of the “Nutcracker”. It has been pointed out that he sometimes lacked the power to develop ideas symphonically, choosing instead an episodic form. But if there are composers more profound, more cerebral, there are also few who have equalled the poignancy of his self-expression. Tchaikovsky’s heart is in his music, and those who approach it with their hearts rather than their brains alone will find much there for themselves.

The “1812” Overture was written by Tchaikovsky in 1880 for a large, outdoor ceremony — something like the “Symphonie Funebre et Triomphale” of Berlioz, also in tonight’s programme. A large church was to be consecrated in Moscow, and for the occasion Tchaikovsky conceived a fantasia which could be played in the public square outside, with orchestra, brass, and even cannon. He decided to glorify the year 1812, the year of Napoleon’s defeat in Russia, since the church had been built as a memorial to the Russian victory. The opening, accordingly, uses a Russian hymn, “God, Save Thy People”; then follows a musical depiction of the Battle of Borodino, where we hear the Russian national anthem and the French Marseillaise locked in combat representing the warring soldiers. Finally the Russian anthem emerges in a brilliant display of musical pyrotechnics, festive fireworks of the highest order.

SYMPHONIE FUNEBRE ET TRIOMPHALE
Hector Berlioz (1803-1869)

Berlioz is best known for his dramatic, dazzling orchestral showpieces — works such as the “Roman Carnival” Overture or the brilliant “Symphonie Fantastique.” He was also a visionary innovator in form, experimenting with various combinations of chorus and orchestra throughout his life; apparently dissatisfied with instruments alone, he turned to soloists and ensembles for additional expressive power, as in his dramatic cantata “Romeo and Juliet.”

The Symphonie Funebre et Triomphale is, in some ways, a step back in style. It was commissioned by the French Minister of the Interior to celebrate the tenth anniversary of the 1830 Revolution. Originally scored for large military band, it was designed to accompany a large-scale, outdoor ceremony; a huge procession was to march through the streets to the Place de la Bastille, where a service honouring those killed in the fighting would be held. The first movement, the Funeral March, was played over and over as the 200 musicians, led by Berlioz (in uniform), headed the parade. The second movement, the Funeral Oration, accompanied the blessing of the clergy; and the finale was to celebrate the triumphs of the Revolution.

Berlioz had long wanted to write a piece of music for such an occasion. There was a whole tradition in France of outdoor spectacles of this sort, dating back to the 1789 Revolution and efforts of the new government to unite the people through impressive rallies. Berlioz had probably heard revolution-inspired compositions of Gosssec and Mehul when he was growing up; and recollections of their work must have urged his composing pen, as he claimed that composition of this Symphonie took him only 40 hours! Still, it is an imposing achievement; rarely heard because of its size (it calls for a minimum of 107 players), the Symphonie has an eerie hypnotic quality from the pervasive sound of the high clarinets and side-drums. The Funeral March is one of the supreme tests of a conductor’s skill; he must keep it moving but also sustain an impression of solemnity and breadth. The Funeral Oration exploits an expressive trombone solo; and the finale (ruined at the premiere in Paris because of some mis-timed maneuvers of the soldiers) ends the work in a blaze of glory.

TWO MOVEMENTS FOR STRINGS
Kok-Ichi Hattori (Born 1933)

After training in Japan, Hattori went on to Michigan State University in America and the Hochschule für Musik in Berlin. He is widely-known in Japan as a composer, writer and producer of music education television programmes. He has also travelled extensively outside Japan, lecturing in Russia, America, the Philippines, and South America. Hattori is also in demand as a conductor, leading his own works and other contemporary compositions in Japan and overseas. The Two Movements for Strings, composed in 1977, are among numerous works Hattori has written for school orchestras and bands.

PRIME OF LIFE
WONG YUK-YEE

Wong Yuk-yee began his music studies in Hong Kong. To widen his horizon in the field of music, he attended the National Music Academy in Hamburg, West Germany in 1960 and majored in composition. He returned to Hong Kong in 1968 and is now faculty members of the Hong Kong Conservatory of Music, the Fine Arts Department of the Hong Kong Baptist College and the Extra-Mural Department of the University of Hong Kong.

PRIME OF LIFE is written in commemoration of the 1979 Asian Youth Music Camp. The bright and energetic subjects portray the warmth and vitality of the young. Different scales and modes are used to present Hong Kong as a meeting point of the East and the West and to describe the new challenges ahead and the bright hopes for the future.

VIOLIN CONCERTO IN A MINOR, BWV 1041
Johann Sebastian Bach (1685-1750)
(Allegro)
Andante
Allegro assai

One of the happiest periods of Bach’s life was the time he spent at the court of Anhalt-Cothen, from 1717 to 1723. There Bach was in the service of music-loving Prince Leopold, who employed 18 musicians in his residence. Officially, Bach was supposed to act as Kapellmeister, of director of music in the royal chapel; in fact, there was no elaborate musical programme for the chapel, and Bach’s duties centred mainly on the secular music, official and not-so-official, which formed so important a part of court life. The Prince maintained an excellent chamber orchestra (apparently the inspiration

=== Page 16 ===
for the Brandenburg Concertos) and he himself played in concerts. Bach and the Prince became close friends; the latter stood as godfather to Bach's first son, and it was with great sadness that Bach returned, years later, to conduct the funeral cantata when the Prince suddenly died.

The two Bach violin concertos were designed for performance at this court, by its relatively small orchestra. The solo part—practically the earliest surviving solo violin concerto in music history—is not quite as brilliant and extroverted as those of the Vivaldi concertos, for example. Instead, Bach was writing for his musically-sophisticated employer, and strove to create a sober and musically substantial work, worthy of the Prince. Still, dance rhythms sneak into the piece, spurring its melodies skyward, and urging its harmonies to blossom with a richness in which Bach has no equal.

The opening movement has no tempo marking in the original manuscript, but by tradition it would be an allegro, with a lively orchestral ritornello which returns to subdivide the movement and round it off at the end. The slow movement, like those of many concertos by Bach, is built over a semi-ostinato figure in the bass, which returns over and over; over this are suspended, like melodic catenaries, the lyric swoops of the solo part. The finale, using a ritornello again, seems to go on without breathing, in a sort of spiritual gigue.

VIOLIN CONCERTO IN D, OP. 61
Ludwig van Beethoven (1770-1827)
Allegro ma non troppo
Larghetto
Rondo

Beethoven composed a fairly large number of concertos, mostly for the piano, his own instrument. Yet he left only one violin concerto, almost as though, in this single work, he had said about all he intended to say on the subject. And he may well have been right; compared to all earlier concertos, this one is a giant, an epic work dwarfing all previous examples. The concerto was the product of a rather unusually happy period in Beethoven's life. He was surrounded by friends, his love life was on an even course, and a succession of masterpieces—including the Fourth Piano Concerto and Fourth Symphony—testify to his good spirits in 1806, the year of composition of the Violin Concerto. And another measure of its good naturedness is its dedication; Beethoven chose to inscribe it to Stephan von Breuning, whose mother had taken Beethoven in as a child. Ludwig and Stephan became, and remained, lifelong friends, collaborating on Fidelio and other works. In all his life, perhaps, Beethoven had no finer friends, and it is only right that he should be thus remembered.

The actual violinist for whom the Concerto was written, however, did not treat it with such respect. Franz Clement, only 26, was the conductor/leader of the Theater an der Wien, where numerous works of Beethoven had their premieres. The Concerto was barely completed in time for the first performance; the ink was still wet, apparently, and moreover the part was laid out on four staves—for easier revision. Revision may have been aided, but Clement's sight-reading was not; apparently the premiere was a bit of a disaster. This was not helped by Clement's rather unusual approach to programming: he played the concerto in two parts, separated by an interval and a group of solos (including a sonata for a single-stringed fiddle played upside down!) Given these antics, no wonder the audience that night dismissed the piece.

It was the great Joachim, and later Fritz Kreisler, who made the concerto as popular as it is now it. It took their crusading to convince the public of the worth of a piece which avoids brilliance for brilliance's sake, and integrates the solo line into a great symphonic development. After the initial hair-raising octaves, the soloist joins the orchestra in the discourse of the first movement; he emerges again in the limelight in the larghetto central movement, which presents him with variations over a hymn-like theme. The rondo more than makes up for this solemnity, with its high-flying (paired, oddly, with a bassoon) and a jovial finale to one of Beethoven's finest creations.

D小調序曲 韓德爾
(1685—1759)
(英國作曲家歐格爾改編)

自一七一八年起，韓德爾受僱於英國貴族贊助士公爵布列節斯宮中為音樂總監，曾作多首合唱及器樂作品，包括著名之十一首「贊美士頌歌」；其中第二首採用聖經中詩篇第九、十一、十二及十三篇為題材，名為「篤信於主」，該頌歌以一莊嚴之序曲開始。

十九世紀末英國作曲家韓德爾仰慕英國維多利亞女王時代之音樂，因受此序曲華貴及輝煌之氣勢所吸引，遂將此原來為巴洛克時代室樂團所寫之序曲重新編訂，配以現代化之器樂效果，使成為一首多姿多采，氣質超卓之作品。

太平山下 林樂培
(生於一九三五年)

林樂培生於澳門，曾赴加拿大大多倫多大學，後期進入南加州大學深造，專攻電影配樂。自一九六四年回港以來，林氏曾致力於音樂創作及提倡香港作品於國際上之地位。其「謝灶」一曲，乃受香港電台委約作成曾於本年度代表參加於巴黎舉行之世界電台聯合作品首播，被選為前十五名。

林氏音樂創作之風格雖為多元化，然其中最特出乃中西音樂技巧之交替運用，其配器手法多姿多采，而充滿戲劇性。「太平山下」為香港音樂事務統籌處本年度委約作品之一。

幻想 金容振
(生於一九三○年)

於韓國出生之金容振，早年肆業於漢城國家大學，獲音樂學士及碩士學位，隨後更往美國紐約及依利諾州深造，回國後任教於漢城國家大學為副教授。

=== Page 17 ===
金氏之重要作品包括有「布拉姆斯頌」（四組絃樂及敲擊合奏），以及管絃樂作品「樂韻」。

金氏作品組織緊密，偶亦採用比較前衛性之手法，純粹以聲音作爲樂曲之依歸。

太陽音樂之三 彼得·史高霍（生於一九二九年）

今年五十歲之澳洲作曲家史高霍曾畢業於墨爾本大學及牛津大學，師承著名作曲家艾文洛伯以及愛堅·華萊斯。自一九六三年以後，史高霍任教於雪梨大學。

澳洲在世界樂壇上近十數年來才漸露頭角，史高霍在音樂創作上之努力，對此實貢獻不少。他曾表示對歐洲音樂無大興趣，自認其創作靈感主要來自澳洲本身之傳統音樂素材。他認爲亞洲之音樂觀念，實對再造及加強西方創作技巧方面，有著莫大幫助。

「太陽音樂」之結構及概念，正表示出史氏論點。在樂曲中，他嘗試不依賴西方自貝多芬以來所慣用之主題發展手法，而採用充滿東方色彩之概念，嘗試純粹以聲音之感覺爲依歸之結構。為達到此目的，他曾說：

「一套全新之樂器運用技巧——微分音及半音之音調由絃樂器及銅管樂器發出，絃樂緩慢不斷之滑音；銅管樂器不同聲量及強弱節拍之和絃互相交替；由五十九個不同之四分一音所組成稠密及閃爍之和絃……以圖創造出一種完全靜止，充滿咀咒性以及嚇人之感覺，這是一種富有強烈色彩之音樂，正像耀眼強光，閃爍燦爛；也許只有像澳洲這樣的一個國家才會孕育出沈澱對光與熱莫名之敵意。」

「太陽音樂」之三雖為中等規模樂隊而寫，然其敲擊樂器部份則被大大增強，並加入了傳統樂器以及一些原始之亞洲音樂聲響。

西班牙狂想曲 夏布里耶（1841－1894）

夏布里耶原是法律界出身，曾服務於巴黎內政部達十八年之久。然他於工餘時間却結交很多當時藝術界知名人士，如印象派大師倫維、曼尼及作曲家科里等。四十歲那年，曾到德國華格納歌劇之都拜奈，受其音樂所感動，遂立志獻獻下生於音樂創作。雖然夏布里耶以後只活多十三年，但仍能創作出大批可以留存千古之美妙作品。

夏布里耶決志之初，首批作品多是鋼琴曲，因他本身對鋼琴演奏素有研究。隨後夏氏到西班牙遊覽，被當地風光所陶醉，回國後遂作成「西班牙狂想曲」。全曲取材自西班牙各地民族舞曲，織有西維爾、格蘭羅特以及亞坎巴等地作品。然全曲最精采之處，是接近完場時伸縮號角所奏出之引人傾耳之樂句——純粹只有夏布里耶才能作出此另人讚嘆之音韻。

菲島掠影 露格里芝雅·加施力

加施力為菲律賓最著名及最受敬仰之作曲家之一，他除了出任國家文化中心之主席外，更常聯絡國內外機構，努力推行音樂事務。

加施力早年於本國大學畢業後，曾留學美國伊士文音樂學院。回國後一直不斷創作，作品總數已達二百多首，形式包括民歌、藝術歌曲、合唱、室樂以及大型管絃樂。

除作曲外，加施力更致力研究發掘及運用傳統亞洲樂器，使能與西方樂器互相配合，達到東西合璧。

「菲島掠影」作於一九七四年，採用菲律賓三個最大島嶼。呂宋、維沙也及閩丹撈之民族音樂為素材。第一樂章「山邊」充滿田野氣氛，有著一般狂想曲的感覺；第二樂章「安眠曲」則比較寧靜，主要由長笛奏出美妙的旋律；最後樂章「節日」描寫一條小村莊的慶典，村民翩翩起舞，強勁的鼓樂聲中，更有欣喜的狂叫。

洋娃娃舞曲 羅永暉（生於一九四九年）

羅永暉生於香港，現年三十歲早年曾留學台灣國立大學攻讀作曲，事師台灣名作曲家許常惠，同港後從事教學工作，並為香港中文大學音樂系之兼任結他導師。一九七七年再赴美深造，隨約翰·歌羅福於美國加州大學研究作曲法，並獲碩士銜。

羅永暉之作品富有創意，像寫於一九七二年之琵琶獨奏曲「竈」混合了傳統及現代手法，用自由調性之材料應用於中國傳統樂器上；又像長笛及結他二重奏曲「桑林調」，採用較前衛之作曲法，但仍不失中國氣氛，該曲被獲選為代表香港參加一九七九年於巴黎舉行之國際新作交流會。

羅永暉最近之作品，包括絃樂四重奏「坐看雲起時」及管絃樂曲「鍵」等，皆採用無調性手法而力求配合中國音樂之韻味。

洋娃娃舞曲是本年特別為香港音樂事務統籌處而寫的作品之一。

A小調低音大提琴協奏曲 多明尼高·德拉高奈

被喻為「低音大提琴中之帕格利尼」之意大利大提琴家兼作曲家德拉高奈自幼即天才橫溢，除於幼年即加入當時著名音樂學府聖馬可大教堂擔任大提琴手外，更不斷創作無數作品。像與他同期之作曲家莫扎特一樣，德拉高奈曾遊歷歐洲列國，最後定居英國，渡過晚年。德氏交遊甚廣，當時著名作曲家海頓是他的摯友，貝多芬在信札中也經常提及他的名字。

德拉高奈生活多姿多采，

=== Page 18 ===
除嗜音樂外，他亦是一收藏家，專門收藏洋娃娃以及當時流行之鼻煙盒；德氏亦愛寵物，每次演出都要令其愛犬卡路坐在身邊。

德拉高奈大約有數百首低音大提琴作品留存於世，原稿現存於倫敦大英博物館中，其中較具特色的乃其改編自巴赫風琴賦格曲之低音部份。今次音樂會所演出之A小調低音大提琴協奏曲，則比較普及，然亦要求高度之演奏技巧，才能使這深厚沈重之樂器現出其罕有華麗之神采。

雙絃樂隊協奏曲 米高·狄貝特（生於一九○五年）

米高·狄貝特被喻為英國當代最具智慧及個性之作曲家，他對自己作品的質素極為重視，精雕細琢，毫不苟且，其作品數量較少，故其知名度有時比不上如布烈頓般的多產作曲家。狄貝特之主要作品包括三套歌劇，一首清唱劇，三首交響曲以及其他管絃樂，合唱，或室樂作品。

狄貝特雖生於倫敦，然他多居於鄉間，對大自然特為喜愛，他亦是一堅定之和平主義者，曾因反對英國參加第一次世界大戰，拒絕服役而被囚三月之久。後來繼著名作曲家賀斯出任著名莫利學院之音樂總監，曾在倫敦安排無數高水準及多姿采之音樂會。

雙絃樂隊協奏曲為狄貝特作品中較受人喜愛的。因採用兩個絃樂隊互相對奏，故作者有更多機會發揮兩者間節奏上及對答上更有趣之想像。絃樂器柔和的音色好像特別引起狄貝特創作旋律之能力，於第三樂章裏，複雜節奏之中由低音部冒出一清新優美之旋律，酷似作者最喜愛之黑人靈歌；隨後樂曲以在一有力的氣氛中結束。

「1812」序曲 柴可夫斯基

世人對柴可夫斯基的評價，往往有兩個不同極端的看法。初接觸古典音樂的人士認爲柴可夫斯基的音樂能給予他們甚至比貝多芬的音樂更大的滿足；而久經訓練的音樂分析家則強調其音樂缺乏完整結構的弱點，而忽略其他好處。

事實上柴可夫斯基音樂真正的地位，應該處於此兩極端之間，而稍偏於初學音樂人士的看法。他的音樂感之人處，往往無人能做效；雖則發自個人之感受，而往往因柴可夫斯基用最簡單，最直接以及強烈的手法表現，所以他的音樂能廣傳於世而贏得後世千萬人之共鳴：例如充滿悲憤心情的第四、第五及第六交響曲，流露真愛的「羅密歐與茱莉葉」交響曲，甜美的A小調三重奏，或是神奇的「胡桃夾子」組曲等。

有人指出柴可夫斯基有時因缺乏音樂發展的技術，退而求助於片段性樂想，不過，雖則有其他作曲家比他更高深及思想更嚴密，然試問又有誰能與他獨到而豪邁的表現力相比？柴可夫斯基把自己的心放進音樂裏，只有用心而不是用理性去欣賞他的音樂，才會領略到個中精采的地方。

「1812」序曲作於一八八○年，像貝利奧斯之「葬禮凱旋交響曲」一樣，同樣為一盛大之室外典禮而作。當時是在莫斯科一間特為紀念俄國於一八一二年擊退侵略者拿破崙而建造之大教堂剛落成時，柴可夫斯基特為此大教堂之祝聖典禮而作了此首隆重之交樂序曲。

樂曲開始時，採用俄國一首聖詩「主救爾民」為題材，中段的音樂則描寫法俄大戰，俄國國歌以及法國之「馬賽進行曲」互相交織；為求達到輝煌迫真效果，更動用數枚大砲於演出時發放；混亂過後，俄國國歌以勝利者姿態再現，全曲於一燦爛光榮之氣氛中結束。

葬禮凱旋交響曲 貝遼士（1803－1869）

法國浪漫期作曲家貝遼士善長於創作大型，戲劇化及燦爛輝煌之管絃樂曲，像膾炙人口之「羅馬嘉年華敘曲」以及著名之「幻想交響曲」等。貝氏亦是一位敢於創新及有遠見之作曲家，他曾嘗試以合唱配合樂隊演出，但仍覺得未表達其內心情感，有時更採用獨唱以及小組合奏配合前兩者，來求增加音樂之表現力，以此手法編寫成的樂曲有著名之大型清唱歌劇「羅密歐與茱莉葉」。

「葬禮凱旋交響曲」從某一角度來說，可算是貝氏比較保守之表現。此曲作於一八四○年，當時貝利奧斯受法國內政部特別委約，為紀念一八三○年之革命而作，樂曲原寫給樂隊演奏，為配合龐大禮儀之進行。全曲共分三樂章，首樂章實為一葬禮進行曲，貝遼士身穿軍服，領導者樂隊及遊行隊伍，浩浩地操進大革命之發源地，巴黎巴士的廣場；第二樂章則為於廣場公開進行之紀念儀式之配樂，莊嚴而隆重；最後一樂章則充滿歡悅氣氛，慶祝大革命之凱旋。

自一七八九年之大革命以來，法國政府一直鼓吹以雄壯而感人之遊行音樂來團結民心，此一傳統，影響貝遼士，他一直以來都渴望能寫一首歌頌國家的作品。「葬禮凱旋交響曲」花去他四十個工作小時，但亦為貝氏罕有之傑作。演奏此曲，所費人力甚大（至少需要樂手一百○七人）然樂曲有著一種令人沈醉而興奮之感覺，強烈而尖銳之單簧管，而及有緊密節奏之大鼓，使聽者不期然跟著音樂踏步前進。

第一樂章之進行曲，對指揮者來說是極具考驗，他一面要維持前進之節奏感，另方面却要表現出樂曲應有之莊嚴及氣魄。在第二樂章裏，伸縮號獨奏配合著儀式之進行，而全曲則在第三樂章輝煌之氣氛中結束。

=== Page 19 ===
絃樂二章　服部公一
（生於一九三三年）

服部公一早年於日本受教育，隨後赴美國密西根州立大學及柏林音樂學院深造，回國後忙於寫作及監製音樂教育之電視節目，為日本著名作曲家之一。

服部公一除活躍於日本樂壇外，更出國講學，足跡遍及蘇聯、南北美洲以及東南亞。服部公一亦專於指揮，常指揮演出自己及日本其他作曲家之作品。

「絃樂二章」作於一九七七年，為服部公一所作衆多為學校樂隊演奏作品之一。

錦繡年華　黃育義

黃育義在香港接受音樂教育，一九六○年赴西德漢堡國立音樂學院深造，主修作曲，一九六八年回港，現任教香港音樂學院、香港浸會學院藝術系及香港大學校外課程部。

「錦繡年華」乃為今次亞洲青年音樂營而作的樂曲，以朝氣蓬勃及精神滿溢的輕快節奏來表達年青人的天真、熱情和充滿活力的錦繡年華。香港是中西文化交流的城市，作者用五聲音階及大小調交替運用，來表達這種現象，更用無調及十二列音音樂的手法來描述年青人與新事物的接觸，以及遠大光明的前程。

A小調小提琴協奏曲
巴哈（一六八五至一七五○）
（快板）
行板
很快的快板

一七一七至一七二三年，巴哈受聘於雷奧博王子為柯坦宮教堂的音樂總監。王子酷愛音樂，聘有十八名音樂家。巴哈主要的工作是為皇宮安排非宗教音樂。王子有一個很好的樂器樂團（這也許是觸發巴哈寫布蘭登堡協奏曲的因素），他自己亦有參加演奏。巴哈與王子是深交，王子是巴哈第一個兒子的教父；日後王子突然逝世，巴哈回到皇宮指揮葬禮的清唱曲。

巴哈兩首小提琴協奏曲都是為柯坦宮的小型樂團寫作。小提琴的獨奏部份——也許是現存樂史中最早的小提琴協奏曲。巴哈努力要寫成一個有深度內涵的音樂作品，以供有高音樂修養的王子欣賞。樂曲中亦偶有舞蹈的節拍，令旋律更加輕快，加強了樂曲的和諧。

原稿中的第一樂章並沒有註明速度，不過依據傳統，這該是快板，輕快的過門將樂章分段及結束。行板就像巴哈其他的協奏曲一樣，以低音爲基礎，反複出現；終曲又再採用不歇斷的過門，聽來有點像格拉舞曲。

D大調小提琴協奏曲　貝多芬
作品編號六十一
（一七七○至一八二七）
從容的快板
甚緩板
迴旋曲

貝多芬協奏曲多為鋼琴而作，但他在其唯一小提琴協奏曲中，盡道心聲，作品水平達到最高峯。

此協奏曲作於一八○六年，乃貝多芬一生中最快樂的時期。他在友誼及愛情方面都順利，事業亦獲成功。貝多芬將這首協奏曲送給拳友史提芬·布魯寧，作爲紀念他與布魯寧一家美好的友誼。

協奏曲首演的演奏者乃二十六歲的克萊曼特，克氏當時任維也納劇院樂團指揮及首席，對此曲未有適當演繹，首演險成鬧劇，及至以後經過姚阿幸及克賴斯勒精采的演奏，此樂曲才流行起來。樂曲獨奏及樂隊融合成爲交響曲，以令人震驚的八度音程開首，隨後獨奏者與樂團互相對答，完成第一樂章。在第二樂章獨奏在甚緩板的中段再次顯露，在一個聖詩般的主題上變奏。第三樂章迴旋曲加進雄心勃勃的獨奏，以歡樂的樂句結束這完美的協奏曲。

=== Page 20 ===
LEE Suat-lien (conductor of the Singapore Youth Chinese Orchestra) was born in Singapore and has been active in the Chinese musical scene for over 10 years. His dedication towards artistic work and his enthusiasm in training the young has won him wide acclaim.

Lee received musical training in Israel. He is now the conductor of the Singapore Youth Chinese Orchestra of the Ministry of Education and of two other orchestras. He is also instructor for Chinese instrumental classes organised by the Ministry. Lee has conducted a series of lectures on Chinese instruments and history of music in the University of Singapore and has also written scripts for musical programmes on radio. He conducted the Singapore Youth Chinese Orchestra in the International Festival of Youth Orchestras held in Switzerland in August 1971. In February 1972, he was leader of the Chinese instrumental music ensemble which went as part of the Singapore National Arts Troupe to the Adelaide Arts Festival in Australia. In 1973, he travelled with the same troupe to Russia. The Singapore Youth Chinese Orchestra toured the Philippines in 1975 under his conductorship. He led another Chinese instrumental ensemble to Japan in August 1977. In August 1979, he was invited to appear in the Oriental Music Festival in Durham. He has also conducted the Singapore Youth Chinese Orchestra and the Chinese Orchestra of the School of Commerce & Industry Alumni Association in many performances in Malaysia.

新加坡教育部青年華樂團指揮李雪嶺先生簡介

李雪嶺，新加坡出生，活躍於華樂界已有十餘年，其對藝術工作之認真苦幹與勉勵後進之熱忱，充分表現出其音樂才華。

李君曾受訓於以色列李克利斯指揮班，現為教育部青年團、人民警察隊華樂團及後備軍協華樂團擔任指揮之職，並兼任教育部華樂訓練班導師。李君曾在新加坡大學主講中國音樂史與樂器講座，並曾為廣播电台音樂雜誌撰寫專稿。

七一年八月，曾出席瑞士舉行之國際青年音樂節，指揮教育部青年華樂團的演出。七二年二月，率華樂小組隨新加坡國家藝術團參加澳洲阿特雷德藝術節，次年且前往蘇聯。七五年，指揮青年華樂團赴菲律賓演奏。七七年八月，率華樂小組前往日本。今年八月，受英國主辦當局之邀請，前往英國德汗（DURHAM）參加「東方音樂節」的演出。此外，也曾多次率領青年華樂團與工商校友會華樂團到馬來西亞演奏。

SINGAPORE YOUTH CHINESE ORCHESTRA

The Singapore Youth Chinese Orchestra was formed in 1970 by the Young Musicians' Society with the aim of promoting and improving the art of music making among the youths.
It started off with a membership of 30. Under the able direction of Mr. Lee Suat Lien, the strength of the orchestra has increased to 120 with 54 senior members and 66 junior members from schools, tertiary institutions as well as youths who are in National Service and those working in private and public sectors. Through the keeness of the members and the hardwork of its conductor Mr. Lee Suat Lien, the Singapore Youth Chinese Orchestra is one of the few groups sought after regularly by TV and radio producers to participate in their programmes. The orchestra consists of a full range of Chinese musical instruments and it has a wide repertoire of traditional Chinese instrumental music as well as modern and local compositions.

This orchestra has constantly served the community at large through participation at cultural shows, rallies, Singapore Youth Festival, Music and Dance Presentations, the Ministry of Culture's Music for Everyone Series and concerts at parks and other public places as well as for schools. Its first trip abroad as musical ambassadors for Singapore was in 1971 when it was invited to participate at the Third International Festival of Youth Orchestra in Lausanne, Switzerland. During their stay in Switzerland, the orchestra was invited by the Mayor of Lausanne to play at the homes of the retarded and orphans which was greatly appreciated by those present. Since then it has made the following overseas performances and goodwill tours:—

1972 — Teeside Music Festival (won the 2nd prize in Folk Music Group).
1973 — Goodwill tour and performances to West Malaysia which was a great success.
1974 — Participation in the Llangollen International Eisteddfod in Wales, UK (The Ensemble won 2nd place in the Folk Group Section).
— Performance in London for the students of Singapore and Malaysia.
1975 — Goodwill tour and performances in the Philippines to foster greater understanding between the ASEAN countries.
1976 — Invitation to perform in Muar, Kuala Lumpur and Penang. A musical workshop was organized on the request of the Chinese orchestra enthusiasts in West Malaysia, to share with our Malaysian neighbours our instrumental expertise.
1977 — Invitation by the Selangor Chinese Assembly Hall to conduct a week-long workshop on Chinese Instrumental Music in Kuala Lumpur. The workshop was a great success and it concluded with the combined 100 strong orchestra performing in an evening of instrumental music.

The Singapore Youth Chinese Orchestra has been actively engaged in promoting Chinese music since its inception in 1970. With the great interest created in schools for Chinese instrumental music, the orchestra has plans to go to schools to give concerts and to conduct workshops for school Chinese orchestra members.

新加坡青年華樂團

新加坡青年華樂團於一九七○年成立，隸屬青年音樂家協會。其目標為推廣青年音樂活動及提高表演水準。成立時有團員三十一人，在李雪嶺先生循循善誘下，團員人數增至一百二十人，包括五十四個高級及六十六個初級團員，來自各中學及大專學院，亦有服軍役及在公共和私人機構中服務的青年。團員及指揮李雪嶺先生努力耕耘，為新加坡青年華樂團建立良好的聲譽，經常獲邀在電視及電台參加演出。樂團樂部包括全部的中國樂器，而曲目除有傳統的中樂外還有現代及新加坡的作品。

樂團經常參加社區活動，如文化表演、大瀝演、新加坡青年節、音樂及舞蹈表演、文化部的大衆音樂節目及在公園、學校和公眾地方舉行的音樂會。一九七一年代表新加坡參加在瑞士LAUSANNE 舉行的第三屆國際青年音樂節，受LAUSANNE 市長邀請往孤兒院和弱智人士之家演奏，在座者皆大表讚賞。隨後曾往外地作以下親善訪問及表演：

一九七二年——TEESIDE 音樂節（獲民樂組第二獎）。
一九七三年——往西馬來西亞成功演出。
一九七四年——參加英國威爾斯LLANGOLLEN INTERNATIONAL EISTEDDFOD（獲民樂組第二名）。
一九七四年——在倫敦新加坡及馬來西亞留學生表演。
一九七五年——往菲律賓親善表演，目的為促進東南亞國家之友誼。
一九七六年——應邀往MUAR，吉隆坡及檳城演出，並與西馬來西亞之華中樂團互相交流。
一九七七年——應邀往吉隆坡為SELANGOR 華人會所主持一星期之中國音樂研習班，非常成功，且組成一百人之樂團表演一晚。

新加坡青年華樂團自一九七○年成立以來不斷為推廣中國音樂盡力，並計劃往學校表演及主持中國音樂研習班。

Hong Kong Youth Chinese Orchestra

Under the conductorship of TONG Leung-tak, the Youth Chinese Orchestra began its weekly rehearsals in July 1978 and gave an inaugural concert on 26th December, 1978. Thereafter it gave regular performances in the various districts of Hong Kong. On 11th February 1979 the Youth Chinese Orchestra joined three other Chinese orchestras in Hong Kong in a "quadraphonic concert". This concert was in many ways the first of its kind in Hong Kong: it was the first time a Chinese music concert was performed in the open air with over 400 players from four orchestras seated in four corners of football pitch (thereby producing a "quadraphonic" sound effect). In addition to playing orchestral music, the orchestra also accompanied a 200-member children choir and 60 dancers in the performance of Chinese songs and traditional dances. This concert was well received by a large audience and has been commented on by critics as one of the most interesting and pioneering ventures of the Office. On 20th April, 1979, the Orchestra visited Macau and gave a public concert at the Teatro Diocesano. It toured the United Kingdom and France this August/September with the Hong Kong Youth Symphony Orchestra and gave very successful concerts.

Since July 1978, the Youth Chinese Orchestra has become the symbol of growth of the rapidly developing cultural scene in Hong Kong. The Orchestra is now the goal of young musicians and the pride of their members. But most important of all, this rapid growth of the Orchestra proved the point - that music is one of the best media through which our young can develop their own artistry and personality; and that irrespective of their race, nationality, age and background, our young people will work together in harmony towards a common cultural objective.

香港青年中樂團

在湯良德之指揮下，樂團於一九七八年七月成立，經五個月之緊湊練習，於同年十二月廿六日舉辦成立音樂會。除經常參加地區性演出外，中樂團曾在七九年二月十一日與香港三個中樂團作四聲道之公開演奏。該形式之音樂會可謂創香港之先河——四個中樂團之團員分別坐於球場的四個角落，以能達到四聲道之效果。除演奏樂曲外，中樂團更為一擁有二百名之兒童合唱團及六十位舞蹈家伴奏。是次演出，觀衆人數達數千名，並獲獲好評，更被認定為統籌處之大膽嘗試及創新之舉。於四月二十日，中樂團訪澳門並在當地之公教大會堂舉行一場音樂會，本年八/九月間，與香港青年交響樂團訪英、法演出，非常成功。

自一九七八年成立以來，青年中樂團已逐漸成爲香港樂壇一股新力量。年青樂手均以能加入該樂團為榮。

從樂團之迅速發展可證明音樂是最佳之娛樂活動之一——透過音樂，青年可以培養他們的藝術所長，及個性，而不論他們的種族、國籍、年齡及背景是否相同，青年人也能和諧地向一共同文化目標邁進。

Notes on selected Chinese music items

The music items rehearsed and performed by the Singapore Youth Chinese Orchestra and the combined Chinese orchestras, dance troupes and chorus from Hong Kong fall into three main categories: classical pieces for solo and ensemble playing, compositions for the Chinese orchestra and music rewritten or re-arranged for accompanying folk dances. The following notes briefly describe selected items in each of the three categories.

Classical items — the music with the longest history is probably Yu Qiao Wen Da (Dialogue). Legend has it that the piece was composed during or before the Song Dynasty (960 – 1280 A.D.). It is one of the best loved compositions for the qin, an ancient instrument. The music is composed in such a way to form the effect of a dialogue between a fisherman and a woodcutter. There are imitations of the sounds of rowing and wood-cutting and the listener could almost visualise the leisurely life of the fisherman and the woodcutter. Another piece is San Liu (Three and six), which is one of the eight most famous tunes of southern China. A composition of the Qing Dynasty (1644 – 1911 A.D.), the crisp and rhythmic melody describes the joyful celebration of a good harvest in a picturesque village setting.

Orchestral pieces — many composers have written programmatic music for performance by a Chinese orchestra. Some describe traditional customs and rural scenes, such as:—

Tai Hua Qiao (The Bride in the Wedding Sedan Chair) — it was customary in the past in many rural areas of Chona for villagers to carry a bride on a sedan chair from one village to another on her wedding day. This piece of joyful folk music, re-arranged now for solo on the suo-na (a double reed ethnic wind instrument) could well have been played by the small instrumental ensemble which would accompany the bride on her ride to her new home;

Liang Xiao (Lunar New Year's Eve) — composer Liu Tian-hua (1895 – 1932 A.D.) is one of the most famous Chinese composers. His er-hu (a two-string bowed

=== Page 24 ===
instrument) compositions are standard studies for virtually every er-hu soloist. Liang Xiao was composed on 22nd January, 1928. The music is of typical southern Chinese flavour. It paints a peaceful picture of a Chinese family happily celebrating New Year's Eve and joyfully awaiting the arrival of the Lunar New Year;

Mei Li Di Xi-Shuang-Ban-Na (The Beautiful Xi-Shuang-Ban-Na) — Xi-Shuang-Ban-Na is the name of a district in the Yun-nan Province. Based on a folk melody, the music describes the life of the hard-working peasants living in the area.

Cao Yuan Xiao Zi Mei (Sisters of the Pasture) — a 1974 composition by Lau Tak-hoi and Wong Yin-chiu, originally for performance by a symphony orchestra. The music describes the life of the nomadic shepherd who live on the pasture of Mongolia.

Others depict various aspects of life in a modern society or in an industrialised city:—

Gang Shui Ben Liu (The Rolling Steel Mill) — a 1977 composition, the Chinese orchestra is used to portray the bustling life in a modern steel mill and the perseverance and dedication of those who work in it.

Xiao Bo Mi (Soccer Fan)

Yu Jia Gu Niang (The Young Lady from the Fishing Village) — these two compositions were written in June 1979 by Tong Leung-tak in commemoration of the holding of the Asian Youth Music Camp in Hong Kong. In the music, Tong describes two familiar scenes in Hong Kong — one on a soccer field with two teams of youngsters playing in a feverish game and the other in one of the many fishing villages around the territory.

You Tian Di Zao Chen (The Oil Field in the Morning) — composer Wong Shue-chiu wrote this piece of music in 1968 and used the Chinese orchestra to tell the story of one day's event at an oil field — sunrise, followed by a song of the workers; then the exhilaration when oil is struck at the field and finally, a chorus sung by those who had a job well done.

Then there are the transcriptions and variations based on folk tunes from the various provinces of China:—

A-La-Mu-Han — A-La-Mu-Han is the name of a beautiful young lady who lived in the Xin Jiang Province — a folk song in her praise;

Dui Hua (The All-season Flower) — a folk tune from the An Hui Province;

Bu-Gu-Niao Jiao Chi Liao (The Cuckoo is late this Spring) — a folk song of the Shan Bei Province, where the farmers were earnestly awaiting the first call of the cuckoo, the arrival of Spring;

Wu-Su-Lei Xiang Dong Liu (The Wu-Su-Lei River flows eastwards) — a folk song of the He-Zhe tribe, who depend on the Wu-Su-Lei River for their livelihood.

Mu Min Xin Ge (Song of the Herdsman) — composed in 1973 by Jian Guang-yi and Wang Zhi-wei for solo on the di-zi (the Chinese bamboo flute), the melody is based on a folk tune from Mongolia. The Mongolians are herdsman and the music describes the peaceful and joyful Mongolians travelling with their herd in the wide pastures of Mongolia.

For the outdoor performance of combined Chinese orchestras, chorus and dance troupes, choreographer Ying Long-ping has arranged a number of Chinese dances, based on music of different background:—

Jian Wu (Sword Dance) — a classical duet of a brother and sister who were performing frontier duties in bright moonlight;

Da Yan Nan Fei (South Fly the Snow Geese) — an episode during the flight of a flock of snow geese towards the south, in search of warmer weather. The flock was blown off course in a snow storm and two young ones lost touch with the main team. The whole flock turned back to search for the lost ones and, as all good stories would end, the young ones were found and they flew on in search of peace and warmth.

Liang Zhu (The Butterfly Lovers) — the dance is based on two extracts from the Butterfly Lovers Violin Concerto which was written in 1958-9 by two young composers attached to the Shanghai Conservatory. The concerto might best be described as a programme-concerto in Chinese idiom, its narrative taken from a classic Chinese Opera story. The first section describes the meeting of Shan Bo, a student, and Ying Tai, who, in order to go off to study, must disguise herself as a boy. Their friendship — her love for him — is sundered as she is called off to rejoin her family. Their parting is symbolised in a doleful violin/ cello duet, as the section ends. In the second section the story unfolds. Ying Tai's family arranges her marriage to a wealthy neighbour. Shan Bo, at last realising all that has transpired, laments and dies of a broken heart. Ying Tai, on the way to her wedding, passes his grave. With a clap of thunder the tomb opens, she hurls herself in, and the two lovers are united in paradise.

And finally, to commemorate the occasion of the 3rd Asian Youth Music Camp, 3 officers of the Music Administrator's Office wrote a song as a dedication to the Asian Youth Music Camp movement, with accompaniment by a Chinese orchestra. The music is written by Tung Tak-leong, with the lyrics by Tong Leung-tak and Lui Ki-ling.

Chorus (translated ad lib):—

Ah! Sing Gloria!
Cheerfully we sing!
We are Asian young musicians.
United as one, cheerfully we sing,
To our friendship,
To our progress,
To advancement.
Through our fellowship we are united.
Joyfully we sing!

=== Page 25 ===
「節目的歡騰」

「鑼鼓震天響，鞭炮沖雲霄
調龍舞獅迎新春，風調雨順年年好」

本曲作於一九七七年春節，樂曲描寫了在中國的傳統節日裏，人們歡度新春的那種熱烈場面。

「巍巍寶塔山」

「巍巍寶塔山，高高入雲天
潺潺延河水，源遠幾千載」

一九七五年劉明沅先生根據一首陝北歌曲改編而成，樂曲描繪了古都延安的壯麗景色，人們過着和平幸福的生活。

「大雁南飛」

「深秋季節裏，大雁南去，在途中遇到了暴風雪。一對小雁受傷失落，它們掙扎飛翔，終於在大雁的護衛下，回到了隊伍，繼續南飛」。一九七九年邢浪平先生用這故事編成舞蹈表現蒙族人民，不畏艱難，勇敢堅強的性格。

「美麗的梭羅河」

「梭羅河水源流長，世世代代熱愛它，河水流不盡，贊歌唱不完」。

「油田的早晨」

這是一首四段體的樂曲。
第一段引子奏出油田早晨太陽初升，鳥鳴花香的景色，接著奏出優美如歌的慢板，使人聯想到大自然的美麗。
第二段為快板，樂曲模仿鑽機聲響徹四方，奏出工人們愉快的勞動心情。
第三段表現更為熱烈，是歡慶油田順利建成的熱鬧場面。
結尾以一個壯麗的進行曲式結束，表現出工程之宏偉及對油田的歌頌。
作者王樹銘，寫於一九六八 年左右。

「阿拉木汗」

這是一首新疆民歌，由謝功成編曲，描繪一個美麗勤勞的姑娘叫「阿拉木汗」。

「對花」

安徽民歌，用了鄉土的風味，歡快的旋律，唱出一年四季人們所最愛戴的花朵。真如歌詞中所說的「一年四季百花開，百花開放人人愛，人人愛來人人戴，姑娘呀小伙子戴起來」。

「滿江紅」

中國南宋名將岳飛是一位傑出的民族英雄。歌曲「滿江紅」是以岳飛的詞譜成一首中國古曲。歌曲表達了英雄「盡忠報國」的偉大胸懷和「還我河山」的必勝信心。

「布谷鳥叫遲了」

陝北民歌描寫農家春耕時節，等待布谷鳥在枝頭上迎春歌的情景。

「關山月」

此曲始見於王賓魯先生「梅庵琴譜」（一九三一年），為梅庵古琴派之名曲。中國民族音樂理論家楊隆勳先生，曾試配以唐代詩人李白的同名詩，以表現古代征人遠戍邊疆的不滿情緒。

「美麗的西雙版納」

雲南民歌，由湯良德改編為樂隊合奏曲。樂曲描繪，雲南美麗的西雙版納（地方名）世世代代居住着傣族人民，他們能歌善舞，勤勞勇敢，如詩似畫的美景，給傣族人們帶來無限的歡樂。

「漁樵問答」

此曲的作者不考。明代「藏春塢琴譜」在此曲解題中引及「紫霞洞考」，倘宋代的「紫霞洞琴譜」實有此曲，則其年代可提前到宋或以前。現存琴譜載有此曲的，最早是明代「杏莊太音續譜」（1560），明清琴譜轉載的極多，為流行最廣的琴曲之一。

此曲前段用悠悠自得的樂句重複或移位再現，形成問答對話的效果。另有些琴聲船和砍木的音調，造成了對漁樵生活的聯想。明揚論「太古遺音」說：「按斯曲，想亦隱君子所作也。因見青山綠水，萬古常新，其間識山水之趣者，惟漁與樵。…………是以金蘭同契，拉伴清談，數治亂，論興亡，千載得失，盡付於漁樵談笑之中矣。」這段話頗足以解釋此曲的含意。

「牧民新歌」

「牧民新歌」作於一九七三年，作曲者簡易勇、王志偉兩位本身也是笛子演奏家。樂曲採用了蒙古族的音調編寫而成。歌曲用曲笛來演奏，曲笛音色優美柔和。
樂曲描繪年青一代的內蒙牧民，在藍色遼闊的天空下，無邊無際的草原上盡情高歌的場面。

「梁祝」

舞蹈採用了小提琴協奏曲「梁祝片斷」（樓台會）及「化蝶」的音樂編成。
故事發生在明末，一對同窗友好，叫梁山伯和祝英台。他們互相敬慕，願做終生伴侶，可是封建的祝員外以父母之命媒妁之言，強行把自己的女兒祝英台許配給有財有勢的馬文才。
樓台會相見後，使梁山伯知情憂鬱而死，當祝英台聞訊後悲切斷腸，終於在祝英台出嫁路過梁山伯的墓前撞墓而死。

=== Page 26 ===
「馬兒啊，你慢些走！」

這是一首家鄉的贊歌，抒情、優美、親切、熱情，是一幅美麗的圖畫：
「馬兒啊，你慢些走，慢些走！我要把這迷人的景色看個夠。肥沃的土地好像浸透了油，良田萬畝好像用黃金鋪就。青山滴翠美如畫，人在畫中鬧豐收…………。」
林蔭小道多清幽，姑娘樓前在刺繡。
路旁的小溪撥動了琴弦，好像為姑娘的歌聲伴奏，晚風揚起了溫柔的翅膀，永遠隨着我的馬兒走。家鄉啊，我愛你多彩的風姿，我想看個夠，總也看不夠。

「阿依莎」

新疆有位美麗的姑娘叫阿依莎。她美麗勤勞。她的歌聲比百靈鳥都好聽。她歌唱能把千年荒山變綠洲，唱歌能使麥穗金黃棉桃大。

「大戰太行山」

樂曲以河南音樂作基調描寫了河南人民為了改變窮山溝為米糧川的那種艱苦奮鬥的精神。

「漁家姑娘」

樂曲描寫居住在香港的漁家姑娘，她們勤勞勇敢，從小隨着父母，迎烈日，踏風浪，生活在海洋上。樂曲以三段體組成（1）姑娘織網（2）出海捕魚（3）滿載而歸。

「奔馳在千里草原」

舞蹈是根據一九七五年王國潼，李秀琪所創作的一首二胡齊奏曲所編成，在那遼闊無際，綠草茵茵，如詩似畫的大草原上，蒙族牧民揚鞭躍馬，奔馳在千里草原上。

「良宵」

作曲者劉天華先生為中國著名中樂大師，生於一八九五年二月四日，卒於一九三二年六月一日。作品計有十首二胡獨奏曲，三首琵琶獨奏曲及一首合奏曲等。其二胡曲更為每個二胡演奏家之必修課，其中以「良宵」、「光明行」、「空山鳥語」最為著名。
「良宵」作於一九二八年一月廿二日，又名「除夜小唱」。樂曲具有江南風味，描寫在除夕之夜，人們合家聚一堂，守歲過年之情景。

「小波迷」

一九七九年六月湯良德先生特意為亞洲青年音樂營演出而作此曲。
樂曲以詼諧的兒歌來表現一群天真活潑的少年，在課餘時間裏，展開了一場你爭我奪的足球比賽。
運動給少年帶來歡樂，促進他們的健康成長，鍛鍊堅強意志。

「草原小妹妹」

這首樂曲由劉德海，吳祖強，王燕樵初作於一九七四年，樂曲描繪了內蒙草原上有一對英雄小姊妹，在一次牧羊時，突然遇到暴風雪，通過她們英雄頑強，不屈不撓的鬥爭，終於戰勝了風雪，保護了羊群。

「洪湖水」

這首樂曲是歌劇音樂改編，描寫了主角凌雲壯志，不畏強暴的崇高品質。

「抬花橋」

這是首民間吹鼓曲。描寫過去鄉村村民在喜慶佳日，奏樂抬轎迎新娘的那種熱鬧場面。

「劍舞」

這是首古典雙人舞，舞蹈表現了一對兄妹，爲了保衛邊疆，在一個月光瑩瑩的夜晚，手執利劍，一邊巡邏，一邊練武的情景。
舞蹈由陳華，林阿梅合編，樂曲由符任之先生編配。

「烏蘇里向東流」

赫哲族人們生活愉快，「莊稼綠油油，遍山種花集，魚兒滿江游，歌聲傳山坡」。
