TRIELYNVAR is for flute, piano and vibraphone. This trio, written for San Diego-based flutist Lynne Schuvert, is loosely speaking, variations on the opening material. The piece begins with a single line in the vibraphone. The flute and piano underscore certain motives of this line by doubling at the unison. This doubling gradually moves away from a pure unison until the texture is quite dense, culminating in a loud, double-time solo for the piano, with a quiet, digital-delay-like canonic closing.

Toshiro Mayuzumi was born in Yokohama 1929 and studied at the Tokyo University of Fine Arts and Music with Kunihiko Hashimoto (1945-1951), and at the Conservatoire Nationale de Musique in Paris under Tony Aubin (1951-52). In 1952 he returned to Japan, founded the group Ars Nova Japonica, and began working with electronic sounds. His style of composition embodies elements from old Japanese music, serial techniques, and electronic sound.

A HALO OF DARK STARS is a concerto for MIDI controller and computer. This virtuosic piece is a huge arch form which opens with a long controller cadenza. I envision the live performer and the computer as having formed a sort of unholy alliance which each performer tries to subvert. Over time each strives to dominate the other, until they once again achieve a certain uneasy balance.

Stravinsky, but a musical tribute in the form of a memoir with only a few passing references to his works: the opening hurly-burly of Petrouchka, a violin solo passage from L’Histoire du Soldat and a fleeting suggestion of the chord spacings of The Rite of Spring. But in all aspects this is an original work, freshly conceived and executed. The “borrowing” of Stravinsky is used in the same way he himself “borrows” from other composers, resulting in an entirely different musical atmosphere and composition. Also, like Stravinsky this work is balletic for it is inspired by the movements of the body in motion.

TWELVE는 로스앤젤레스의 Monday Evening Concerts Series에서 초연되었다. 이 곡의 제목은 이 작품에서의 “마이크로 구조”와 “메트로 구조”에서 작용하는 원리를 설명해 주고 있다. 이 곡에서 사용된 12개의 악기와 12개의 악장 구성, 그리고 12개의 음에 의한 음고구성 등은 이 음악과 관련을 가지고 있기도 하다. 그 외에도, 이 곡은 재즈의 특성을 가진 것과도 관련을 가지고 있을 뿐만 아니라, 조성적 경향과 관련을 가지고 있다. 각 악장은 다음과 같다:

Robert Linn was born in San Francisco in 1925 and studied composition with Darius Milhaud, Halsey Stevens, Roger Sessions and Ingolf Dahl. He is Professor of Music and Chairman of the Music Theory and Composition Department at the University of Southern California. He is President of the National Association for American Composers and Conductors, Los Angeles Chapter.

His many published compositions include works for symphony orchestra, wind orchestra, chorus, and chamber ensembles. Recent recordings include Concertino for Violin and Wind Octet, featuring violinist Eunice Shapiro and conductor William Kraft; Dithyramb for Eight Cellos performed by "I Cellisti" and commissioned by the American String Teacher's Association in honor of Pablo Casals; Quintet for Woodwinds played by the Westwood Wind Quintet; Vino for violin and piano interpreted by Harris Goldman and Carolyn Brown; Saxifrage Blue for baritone saxophone and piano, commissioned and performed by Mark Watters; Quintet for Brass Instruments played by the Fine Arts Brass Quintet; Duo for Cello and Piano performed by Nancy Yamagata and Mary Au; and Quartet for Saxophones featuring the Eugene Rousseau Saxophone Quartet.

TWELVE was premiered on the Monday Evening Concerts Series in Los Angeles, California. The title of the piece describes an organizational principle at work in both the micro-and macro-structure of the music. An ensemble of twelve instruments, twelve movements, and pitch organization of twelve tones indicate some of these musical references. In addition, there is a concern for tonal orientation of the materials, as well as an adaptation of jazz characteristics. The movements are marked:

1. Prelude 2. Dance 3. Canon 4. Chaconne #1 (woodwind quartet and piano) 5. Intermezzo (violin and cello) 6. Chaconne #2 (brass trio and percussion) 7. Arioso 8. March 9. Ostinato 10. Cadenza 11. Finale 12. Postlude

The piece is scored for flute, oboe, clarinet, bassoon, horn, trumpet, trombone, violin, cello, contrabass, piano and one percussionist.

IDEA AND IMAGE 는 <형식>과 <영역>의 조합이다. 작곡가 마 슈이롱은 중국 시의 형식으로부터 얻은 아름다움의 영상을 전해준다. 이 작품에서 우리는 無와 有의 상호관계, 즉 互助論을 엿볼 수 있다. 無는 有를 내포하고 있고 有는 無를 표현한다. 작곡가는 <직관적 형식>으로 <교묘한 정식>과 <분명한 영역>을 우리에게 선사하는 것이다.

Shui-Long Ma was born in Keelung, Taiwan, in 1939. He studied Theory and Composition under Professor Hsiao Erh-Hua at the National Taiwan Academy of the Arts and graduated in 1964. He was awarded a scholarship in 1972 to study under Dr. Oscar Sigmund in Regensburg Kirchenmusik Hochschule, West Germany, and graduated with distinction in 1975. Mr. Ma has won many awards for his compositions, among them the Sun-Yat Sen Literature and Arts Award, and the Wu-San Lien Literature and Arts Award.

His compositions are of wide range, including works for orchestra, chamber ensemble, piano solo, solo voice, and chorus. He has arranged many Chinese folk songs for chorus and piano accompaniment. His works have been performed in Taiwan, Europe, the U.S., South Africa, and Southeastern Asia.

At present, Mr. Ma is Dean of Academic Affairs and Professor in the Department of Music, National Institute of the Arts. He also serves as the Executive Director of the Republic of China National Committee, is a member of the Asian Composers League, and is the Music Member for the Council for Cultural Planning and Development of the Executive Yuan.

IDEA AND IMAGE is the combination of Form and Realm. The composer, Shui-Long Ma, conveys the imagery of beauty from the Chinese poetic form, and reflects it upon the creative idea. In this piece we find interaction between Void and Solid, the beauty of mutualism: Void connotes Solid, and Solid reveals Void. The composer inventively presents us the beauty of clever-quietude and clear-realm through the intuitive form.

임우상 (林友相)은 계명대학교 음악대학 및 동 교육대학원을 졸업했으며, 캘리포니아주립대학교 (L.A.)에서 수학하였다. 그는 6회의 작곡발표회를 가진 것을 비롯하여, 제4회 서울음악제, 창악회, 한국작곡가회, 아시아작곡가연맹의 작곡발표회에서도 많은 작품을 발표하였다.

작품활동 이외에도, 그는 한국작곡가협회 대구지부장을 역임하는 동안 여러 차례의 작곡발표회와 작곡창출을 개최하는 등, 대구 지방의 작곡활동에 큰 역할을 담당하였다. 또한, 그는 創友會와 한국음악협회 대구 지부장을 역임하는 동안 지방악단에 기여한 공로와 활발한 창작활동 등으로 경북문화상을 수상하기도 하였다.

주요작품으로는 현악4중주곡을 비롯하여, 여러가지 현성의 실내악곡, 가곡집「枯木」등의 가곡들, 합창곡, 그리고 관련악곡 등이 있다. 그는 창악회, 아시아작곡가연맹 한국위원회, 한국작곡가협회, 創友會, 대명양작곡가회 등의 회원으로서 활발한 작품활동을 하고 있으며, 또한 한국음악학회 부회장을 맡고 있다. 현재 계명대학교 음악대학 작곡과 교수로 재직하고 있다.

관현악을 위한 “山景”은 1988년 캘리포니아 州立大學校 (Los Angeles)에서 1년간 연구하는 동안 작곡한 것으로서, 3管編成으로 되어 있다. 특히 이 곡에서는 많은 종류의 타악기들이 사용되고 있다.

이 곡의 중심을 이루는 요소들은 水平의 면으로서의 持續音들과 垂直의 면으로서의 여러 음들의 番積된 合成음으로 구성되어 있다. 더욱이 여러 악기들이 持續音을 이어나가는 동안 겹쳐지는 垂直의 음들의 音群은 소수 악기들에 의한 長・短2度의 番積과 4度, 5度의 合成音으로 이루어지고 있으며, 여러 악기들에 의하여 점차적으로 진행되어가면서 겹쳐지는 全音音階의 垂直의 音量은 強弱과 音色의 調和로 나타나고 있다. 또 한편으로는 타악기를 빈번히 사용함으로써 持續音에 대한 對比의 웅장함과 強烈함을 나타내고 있다.

이 곡의 중심적인理念은 韓國美와 韓國의 民族性에 바탕을 두고 있으며, 아울러 山에 대한 慎懐心, 山景의 神秘性, 그리고 山의 아름다움과 거대함에도 염두를 두었다.

Woo-Sang Lim, a professor at the Department of Composition, College of Music, Keimyung University, is a graduate of Keimyung University and the Graduate School of Education. In addition to his six individual recitals, his numerous works have been premiered through major composition recitals such as the Fourth Seoul Music Festival, regular composition recitals by the Contemporary Music Society in Seoul (CMSS), Korea National Society for Composers, Asian Composers League (ACL), etc.

He served as president of the Daegu chapter of the National Association of Composers in Korea, where he has played an active part in the development of the composers' society in the Daegu area, presenting composition competition sev-

=== Page 27 ===
eral times. Professors Lim was awarded the Kyungbuk Cultural Prize for his vigorous activities and contributions to music in the Daegu area while he was president of Chang Woo Hoe and the Daegu chapter of the Korea National Society of Musicians.

His works include a string quartet, chamber works, songs, including a song collection Withered Tree, choral works and orchestral works. He is a member of several composers' organizations such as the Contemporary Music Society in Seoul (CMSS), Asian Composers League (ACL), Chang Woo Hoe, the National Association of Composers in Korea, and the Pacific Contemporary Music Center. He is also vice-president of the Korean Musicological Society.

MOUNTAINScape FOR ORCHESTRA was written while the composer was a visiting scholar at California State University at Los Angeles in 1988. It requires a large orchestra and a great amount of percussion.

The work's principal elements are "sustaining tones" in the horizontal domain, and "complex sounds" accumulated with various tones in the vertical domain. Groups of tones are formed by combining overlapping verticals with sustained tones, resulting in the accumulation major and minor seconds as well as the more complex sounds of fourths and fifths. Volumes of vertical sound piled up by various instruments progressing step by step are obtained by the symmetry between stress and timbre. In addition to these combinations, frequent use of percussion supplies a magnificent contrast and intensity among sustained tones. The central idea of this work is based on the beauty and the characteristics of Korea.

The composer writes: "I kept in mind yearning for the mountain, the mystery of the mountainscape, and the beauty and immenseness of the mountain as well."

드미트리 스머노프는 1948년 민스크에서 오페라 가수 가족 사이에 태어났다. 그는 1967년부터 1972년까지 모스크바 음악원에서 니콜라이 시텐리노프, 에디슨 데니소프, 유리칸단 코포포프 등과 공부했고, 그 후에 Sovetsky Kompozitor출판사의 편집인으로 일하다가, 1980년부터는 작곡에만 전념하게 된다.

스머노프는 영국의 시인겸 예술가 윌리엄 브레이크의 작품에 감명받아 음악으로 만들었다는 것으로 알려져 있는데, 그 예로는 오페라 <Tiriel>과 <The Lamentation of Thel>, 성악곡<The Seasons> (이것은 그는 후에 제1 교향곡으로 발전시킨다), 그리고 Nash Ensemble 이 1989 년 Almeida축제에서 연주하기 위해 위촉한 <The Moonlight Story>가 있다.

드미트리 스머노프는 작곡가 엘레나 피소파와 결혼했다.

제1교향곡, "SEASONS"작품30번 (1980) — 윌리엄 브레이크 (1757—1827)를 기념하며—: 스머노프는 영국의 환상시인인 윌리엄 브레이크의 작품들에 커다란 매력을 느껴왔다. 그는 브레이크의 시에서 영감을 얻은 많은 작품을 썼는데, 이들 중에는 인성(人聲)과 오르간을 위한 "여섯개의 브레이크의 시" 작품32 (1981)가 있다.

이 곡은 스머노프가 브레이크의 시에 곡을 붙인 것들 중 최초의 주요 작품이다. 1979년 스머노프는 브레이크의 시에 곡을 붙였는데 (영어로 된 시로서, 작곡자 자신의 직접 러시아어로 번역했음) 이 음악이 인성과 앙상블을 위한 곡, <The Seasons, 작품28>이다. 그는 이 곡을 작곡하는 동안에도 이 음악을 전개시키기 위하여서는 음악의 소재가 더 많은 범위를 필요로 한다는 것을 인식했으며, 따라서 그 이듬해 연가곡인 작품에서의 소재를 개작하기 시작하여 「제1교향곡」 작품30(일명 The Seasons)의 기초를 형성하기에 이르렀다. 이 교향곡은 이곡의 모체인 연가곡에서 나타나는 소재들로부터 만들어지고 있 다.

Dmitri Smirnov was born in Minsk in 1948 into a family of opera singers. He studied at the Moscow Conservatory between 1967 and 1972 with Nikolay Sidelnikov, Edison Denisov, and Yuri Khopolov and subsequently worked as editor of Sovetsky Kompozitor Publishers before devoting himself full-time to composition in 1980.

Mr. Smirnov is particularly noted for his works inspired by the English poet and artist William Blake, including the operas Tiriel and The Lamentation of Thel, and The vocal settings The Seasons (later expanded into his First Symphony), and The Moonlight Story, commissioned by the Nash Ensemble for the 1989 Almeida Festival.

Dmitri Smirnov is married to the composer Elena Firsova.

FIRST SYMPHONY, THE SEASONS, op. 30 (1980) In Memory of William Blake (1975—1827): Smirnov has been much attracted to the writings of William Blake, the visionary English poet. He has composed a number of pieces inspired by Blake, including Six Blake Poems, opus 32 (1981), for voice and organ.

It was Smirnov's first major Blake setting that led to his First Symphony. In 1979 he set four Blake poems (in English, and in his own Russian translation) devoted to the four seasons for voice and ensemble (the Seasons, Opus 28). Even as he was working, he realized that the material

=== Page 28 ===
needed more scope for development, so the following year, he reworked material from the song cycle to form the basis of his First Symphony, Opus 30, entitled "The Seasons", and bearing the dedication "In Memory of William Blake (1757-1827)." The symphony grows out of the materials as they appeared in the original song settings. The composer has requested that we reprint Blake's Poems here, not so much as a formal program to the music, but as a guide to its moods and expressive qualities.

김병곤 (金炳坤)은 대구 출신이며, 1961년 미국 인디애나 주립대학교로 작곡과 지휘를 연구하기 위해 떠나기까지, 그는 이미 국내에서 피아니스트·지휘자로서의 경력을 쌓았었다. 인디애나 주립대학교에서 그는 음악석사와 박사학위를 Magna Cum Laude로 받았다.

김병곤씨는 1986년, 서울시립교향악단 미군 순회연주를 위해 동교향악단으로부터 위촉을 받아「初夏」을 썼으며, 이 작품은 뉴욕 (링컨센터), 화성 (케네디센터), 시카고, 샌프란시스코, 로스엔젤레스 등지에서 연주되었다. 이 곡은 뉴욕타임즈紙를 위시하여 미국 각지의 대표지들의 격찬을 받았다. 1988년 서울 올림픽 위원회와 KBS교향악단의 위촉으로 올림픽 축하예술제를 위한「축제 교향곡」을 썼으며, 이 곡은 본인의 지휘로 1988년 서울에서 초연되었다. 1986년에는「十字架上の七言」, 1985년에는 예술살롱에서 개최된 제2회 세계라트협의회를 위해서「하프를 위한 소리」(해코드 출판)등을 썼다. 그리고 서울과 세계 각지에서 연주된「碑銘」(1985년),「陰陽交響曲」(1983년)과 일본에서 해코드로 출판된「오케스트라를 위한 소리」등을 썼다. 그는 또한 위촉작품을 많이 쓴 작곡가로 알려져 있기도 하다.

김병곤씨는 또한 지휘자로서도 한국의 청중들에게 잘 알려져 있다. 그는 서울시립교향악단, KBS교향악단, 대구 시립교향악단 등을 비롯하여 많은 악단은 재현지휘한 바 있다. 1986년에는 중국정부가 조정한 첫 외국 작곡가로서, 北京, 上海, 西安 등지에서 자신의 음악을 소개하고, 그곳의 교향악단을 지휘했다.

1986년에는 폐지적현대음악센터를 L.A.에 창립하여 이 지역 작곡가들의 작품교류, 교환과 연주와 축전에 힘을 기울이고 있다. 현재 캘리포니아 주립대학교(L.A.)작곡과의 책임을 맡고 있다. 그는 또한 동대학교에서 「최우수 교수상」을 받는 등, 많은 포장을 받기도 했다.

신포니에타는 서울 바로크오케스트라의 委屬에 依해 1987년 3月에 完成되어 金受團長과 團員에게 현정된 曲이다. 여기에서 신포니에타(小交響曲)란 이름은 "小"規模란 뜻이 아니고, 作曲家의 本樂團에 對한 感情을 表現하는 愛稱의 뜻으로 사용된 것이다. 이曲은 3樂章構成, 18分의 演奏時間을 갖는 長장하고 큰 曲이다. 16名의 獨走者를 前提로 작曲되었다.

迫力에 넘치고, 素朴하면서, 의젓한 気象을 가진 第1樂章은 double stop과 潤音과 그리고 韓國音樂固有의 音樂語法인 頭音節強拍을 쓴 疊複한 리듬으로 짜인 ベスの音악이다. 이와같은 枝的素材를 積み없이 發展시켜 除除히 展開되어가는 音樂的情景 가운데서, 능동하고, 올바르며, 굳건한 気象을 表現하고자 하는 것이 第1樂章이다.

대조적인 第2樂章에서는, 獨奏와, 音雲을 背景으로 交錯하는 3重奏로서, 楽的 美를 精巧하며, 纖細하게 表現한다. 感嘆의 人絃의 音色을 大きく 為解, sul ponticello(브라지근처에서 연주하는 운궁법), sul tasto(브리지에서 멀리 떨어진 지권위를 연주하는 운궁법), jete(함이 현 위로 떠오른 스타카토)의 技法과 弱音器 사용을 널리하고 있다.

第3樂章은 輕快하며 前進的惰性에 넘치는, 거의 直線的樂章이다. 積み없이 變奏하는 主題는, 現行하는 音樂의 줄거리와는 無關하게, 자주 導入되어 對照, 對位, 相剋을 이루고, 심지어는 원 호흡을 代置해버리는 二律性을 이룬다. 二律性의 원칙은 前後하여 順次의으로 나타남 뿐 아니라, 同時에 使用되기도 하며, 無秩序하게 폭발하는 클라이막스까지 이끌어 간다.

이 作曲家의 音樂은 그 뿌리는 韓國傳統音樂의 美學에 두고 있다. 그는 音樂의 根源의 素材를 韓國語의 言語學的 特徵에서 探索하여, 그것으로 音樂語法의 核分子로 하여, 그의 音樂世界를 展開하고 있다. 積み없이 變化하기는 이 枝的素材로서 漸長과 強弱의 曲線과, 구미치는 感傷과 영동한 韻의 무지개로 이 曲은 構成되었다. 이 作曲家가 重要하다고 느끼는 表現力의 増進과, 聽衆과 對話의 成就를 위하여 그는 可能한 모든 技法을 구에없이 使用하고 있다.

Byong-kon Kim was born in Taegu, Korea. After many active years as a pianist and conductor in his homeland, he moved to the U.S.A. in 1961 to study composition and conducting. He received his M.A. and Ph.D. from Indiana University with high honors.

His Sinfonietta, commissioned by the Korea Chamber Ensemble, was premiered in 1988 at the Opening Conert of the Performing Arts Center in Seoul, Korea and has been released on compact disc. Choyop, commissioned by the Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra for its U.S. tour in 1986 and premiered at the Lincoln center in New York, has enjoyed great success in its many performances around the world. Other recent works include the Festival Symphony (1984), the Sori for Harp (1985), and The Seven Last words of Christ for

=== Page 29 ===
organ and percussion (1986).
Byong-kon Kim has been a frequent guest conductor on the podiums of the Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra, the Korea Philharmonic Orchestra, the Osaka Philharmonic Orchestra, the Daegu Symphony Orchestra, and has toured the People's Republic of China, conducting orchestras in Beijing and Shanghai. Kim was Music Director of the Seoul Chorale of Los Angeles, and has been the Director of the New Music Ensemble of California State University, Los Angeles, since he founded the Ensemble in 1972.
He founded the Pacific Contemporary Music Center in Los Angeles to promote dissemination, exchange, and performance of works by composers from the countries of the Pacific Rim. He is on the faculty of the Department of Music at California State University, Los Angeles.

SINFONIETTA was completed in March of 1987. It was commissioned by the Korean Chamber Ensemble and is dedicated to Min Kim, the director, and the musicians of the Ensemble. The title implies the composer's fondness for the Ensemble rather than a diminutive meaning. In fact, the composition is rather long and magnificent in expression. The piece was written for 15 solo strings and a harpsichord.
The forceful, ragged and vibrant first movement is full of double stops, glissandi and accents in a polyrhythmic texture. A noble, straightforward and expansive mood is pursued in the movement with increasing metamorphoses of the slowly evolving musical events based on a the nuclear materials. The second movement explores thin texture and linear interplay on a cushion of sound in the ground. Subtle string colors are explored in this delicate and exquisite movement. The vivid and forward-moving third movement evolves continually from the beginning to the end. Constantly modified previous statements are recalled to juxtapose, encounter or interrupt an ongoing musical event. This dichotomy, simultaneously or horizontally, leads to chaotic climaxes.
The composer's philosophy is deeply rooted in the aesthetics of traditional Korean music. His intuitive urge to take off on his musical adventures from the very origin of musical sound in linguistic elements led him to adopt such nuclear building blocks as tremolos, glissandi and head-thrust-accent in musical phrases. The ideas are freely used to create a contour of tension and relaxation, changing mood and a sonorous rainbow.
Expressiveness and the communicative quality of music, which are very important to the composer, are pursued through whatever means are available to him. This piece was released in a CD recording in 1989.

조지 유아사는 일본의 고리야마에서 태어나 독학을 한 작곡가이다. 그가 동경의 게이오대학 음예과 학생으로 있을 때 음악에 심취하여 마침내 음악에 모든 것을 다 바치게 된다. 유아사는 1981년부터 샌디에고소재의 캘리포니아 대학 교수로 있다.
1950년대부터 유아사는 관련악곡, 실내악곡, 합창곡, 국음악 및 컨트류 음악등 다양한 악기편성으로 폭넓은 작품 활동을 해 왔다. 그는 또<Prix Italia (1966, 1967)>, <Jurie's Special Prize of the Berlin Film Festival (1961)>, <San Marco Golden Lion Felw owship (1968-69)>등 여러가지 상과 연구지원비를 받았다. 그는 샌디에고 소재의 캘리포니아대학의<Center for Music Experiment> (1976)를 비롯, <Berlin Artist Program (1976-77).>, 시드니에 있는 <New South Wales Conservatorium of Music (1980)>, <University of Toronto (1981)>등에 상주 작곡가로 있었다.
조지 유아사는 <Koussevitzky Music Foundation>, <Saarland Radio Symphony Orchestra>, <Japan Philharmonic Orchestra>, <NHK Symphony Orchestra>, <Canada Council>, <Suntory Music Foundation>, <IRCAM>, <Expo '70>으로 부터 교향악, 실내악, 합창곡, 전자음악등을 위촉 받았다.
유아사는 또 하와이의<Festival of the Arts (1970)>, 브로드의 <New Music Concerts (1980)>, 홍콩의 아시아작곡가연맹(1981)을 비롯하여 British Arts Conuncil의 <Contemporary Music Network> 연주여행, 뉴질랜드에서의 <Asia Pacific Festival (1984)>, 암스테르담에서의 <Composer's Workshop (1984)> 등에 작곡가 혹은 연사로 초청되었다.

현악4중주를 위한 프로젝션은 1970년 "예술과 금세기를 위한 페스티벌"을 위하여 위촉되었으며, 줄리아드 멤버들에 의하여 하와이에서 초연되었다. 이 작품은 12개의 부분들이 결합되어 하나의 악장을 형성하고 있다. 작곡자는 이 곡에 대하여 다음과 같이 적고 있다: "이 작품에서 사용된 원리는 수많은 음향들이 하나의 음향으로 동등화 될 수 있으며, 또한 그 역으로도 될 수 있다는 것이다. 이 원리는 다음과 같은 방법으로 나타날 수 있다. 즉, 어떠한 단일 음향이라도 복합적 음향(단일 음향의 화성적 스펙트럼)의 요소를 가지고 있기 때문에, 단일 음향이라 하더라도 그 자신의 텍스처를 가지게 되는 것이다.
이 작품에서 나는 몇가지 새로운 연주기법을 발전시켰

=== Page 30 ===
Joji Yuasa, born in Koriyama, Japan, is a self-taught composer. While a pre-medical student at Keio University in Tokyo, Yuasa became interested in Music, eventually devoting all his time to the study of composition. Mr. Yuasa has been a Professor at the University of California, San Diego since 1981.

Since the 1950s Yuasa has been active in a wide range of compositional media: the orchestra, chamber, chorus, theater, electronic and computer music. He has been the recipient of many Prizes, awards, and fellowships, including the prix Italia in 1966 and 1967, Jurie's Special Prize of the Berlin Film Festival(1961), San Marco Golden Lion Fellowship(1968—69). He was Composer-in-Residence at the Center for Music Experiment at the University of California, San Diego (1976), Berlin Artist Program (1976—77), the New South Wales Conservatorium of Music in Sydney (1980), and the University of Toronto (1981).

Joji Yuasa has received numerous commissions for his orchestral, chamber, chorus and electronic compositions including commissions by the Koussevitzky Music Foundation, Saarland Radio Symphony Orchestra, Japan Philharmonic Orchestra and NHK Symphony Orchestra, Canada Council, Suntory Music Foundation, IRCAM and Expo '70. As a guest composer and lecturer, Yuasa has participated in the Festival of the Arts in Hawaii(1970), New Music concerts in Toronto(1980), Asian Composers League in Hong Kong (1981), concert tour for Contemporary Music Network by the British Arts Council(1981), Asia Pacific Festival in New Zealand (1984), and Composer's Workshop in Amsterdam(1984).

PROJECTION FOR STRING QUARTET which was commissioned for the 1970 "Festival of the Arts of this Century," was premiered in Hawaii by members of the Juilliard Ensemble. The principle which I used in this composition is one by which many sounds may be equated with one sound and vice-versa. This may be exemplified in the following way: Since any single sound has a component of complex sounds (its harmonic spectrum) even a single sound has its own texture.

In Projection, I developed several new playing techniques, one of which is the rubbing of the bow up and down the deflected strings. Besides the acquisition of new sound materials by these techniques, my main concern in the composition of this piece was with forming a tightly-knit, homophonic sound through the integration created by blending instruments that use identical techniques simultaneously."

프랭크 캠포는 1927년 뉴욕에서 태어났으며 오랜 세월 동안 남가주 지방에 살았다. 그는 로스엔젤레스에서 인골프 디에게 사사했고, 파리에서는 아더 오네지에게, 토플 브라이트 장학금으로 로마 유학을 한 당시에는 고프레도 페드라씨에게 작곡을 배웠다. 1968년에는 남가주 대학에서 음악 박사학위를 받았다.

그의 작품으로는 오페라<The Mirror>, 3개의 간타타, 피아노, 바이올린, 바순, 트럼펫 협주곡 각 하나씩, 다수의 관현악, 피아노 작품들, 성악곡, 그리고 다양한 악기 배합의 실내악 작품들이 있다. 많은 그의 작품들이 음반으로 나와 있으며, 현재는 노스리지 소재 캘리포니아 주립대학에 작곡 및 이론과강으로 재직하고 있다.

실내오케스트라를 위한 세레나데는 1983년 캘리포니아의 몬테시토에서 완성되었다. 악기편성은 각각 2개씩의 목관악기군과 4개의 금관악기, 1명의 타악기 주자, 피아노, 그리고 혼합합주로 되어 있다.

이 곡에서는 5개의 음(F, C, E*, C#, A)으로 이루어진 모티브로 시작하는데, 이 모티브가 이 곡 전체를 통일시켜 주는 요소로서의 역할을 담당하게 된다. 즉, 이 곡의 다섯 개의 악장들은 차례로 이 모티브에서의 음들을 하나씩 사용하여 시작하고 또한 마치게 된다. 말하자면, 제1곡은 F음으로, 제2곡은 C음으로, 제3곡은 E*음 등으로 시작하고 끝나게 되는 것이다. 이 곡의 또다른 구성방법은 마치 시시이 움직이는 방법과 흡사한 것으로서, 각 악장은 그 이전 악장에서 가져온 모티브의 요소(혹은 또다른 부차적인 요소)에 바탕을 두고 있다. 따라서 제2곡은 <Vision>은 제1곡 <Preludio>에서의 요소에, 또한 제3곡 <Interludio>은 제2곡에서의 요소에 각각 바탕을 두게되며, 나머지 악장들도 이와 마찬가지의 방식으로 구성된다. 제5곡은 <Final>은 제4곡 <Musicanotturna>에서 취해온 요소를 사용하게 되는데, 제1곡은 제5곡과 관련을 맺게 됨으로써 제5곡은 원형(圓形)을 완성하게 된다. 그렇지만 아니라, 시작부분에서부터 둘연한 점단되듯이 짧막한 Interludio는 제5곡에서 Coda로서 귀하게 되어 이 곡에서 종결적인 점점을 보다 효과적으로 유도하게 된다.

이 곡은 작곡자가 이탈리아의 베니스에서 장기 체류하던 시기에 처음으로 작성되고 스케치되었다. 이 작품은

=== Page 31 ===
어떠한 의미에서든지 표제적이지는 않지만, 빛나는 도시의 광채와 색채가 이 곡에서 영감의 자료로서 사용되었다는 것은 부정할 수 없을 것이다.

Frank Campo, born in New York city in 1927, is a long-time resident of Southern California. He studied composition with Ingolf Dahlin in Los Angeles, with Arthur Honegger in Paris and with Goffredo Petrassi in Rome while on a Fulbright Scholarship.

In 1968 he was awarded the Doctor of Musical Arts degree by the University of Southern California.

His compositions include an opera, The Mirror, three secular cantatas, four concertos including on each for piano, violin, bassoon and trumpet, a large amount of orchestral music, works for piano, for violin, bassoon and trumpet, a large amount of orchestral music, works for piano, for voice and a wide variety of chamber music for diverse combinations of instruments. Much of his music is available on recordings. He is currently Chairman of Composition and Theory at California State University, Northridge.

SERENADE FOR CHAMBER ORCHESTRA was composed in 1983 and completed at Montecito, California. The work is scored for woodwinds in pairs, four brass, one percussionist, piano and string orchestra.

The opening motive of five pitches (F, C, E flat, C sharp, A) serves as a unifying element throughout the entire work. Each of the five movements, in turn, begins and ends with one of those pitches; thus movement I begins and ends with F, movement II with C and so on. The Serenade is further organized in a chain-like manner with each movement being based on some motivic element (often secondary) taken from the previous movement. Thus the second movement (Visione) is based on elements of the first (Preludio), while the third (Interludio) is in turn based on material borrowed from the second. The Finale employs material from the fourth movement (Musica notturna) and serves to complete the circle as is also related to the first. In addition, the brief Interludio which is initially rather abruptly cut short, now returns as a coda to the Finale and leads to a more conclusive climax.

The Serenade was first conceived and sketched out during a lengthy stay in Venice, Italy. Although the music is in no sense programmatic, the lights and colors of that luminous city did undeniably serve as source of inspiration.

오숙자 (吳淑子): 서울에서 태어난 그녀는 12살 때부터 바이올린을 시작하여 경희대학교 음악대학 기악과에 입학하였으며, 대학3학년 때부터 작곡공부를 하여 1971년 경희대학교 음악대학을, 1973년 동대학원을 졸업하였다.

서울음악제와 아시아작곡가연맹의 음악제에서 수차례 입선하여 일본, 태국, 대만 등 동남아 여러나라에서 작품을 발표하였고, 1976년 미국 피바디음대에서 Jean Ivy 박사에게서 전자음악을 공부하였다. 1979년에는 팔츠부르크 모차르트 국제아카데미에서 Milan Horvart교수에게서 지휘를 공부하였다.

1981년 호주 현대음악제에서 작품을 위촉받아 시드니 교향악단에 의하여 관련악곡 「덧뵈기」를 발표하였고, 1982년 이태리 로마에서 개최된 세계여성작곡가제전에 입선하여 피아노와 타악기를 위한 「무악」(巫樂)을 발표하기도 했다.

그녀는 현재 한국작곡가협회 이사, 한국음악교육자협회 이사 등의 직책을 맡고 있다.

관련악곡, 협주곡, 실내악곡, 가곡집 등 14개의 작품집을 출판하였으며, 독주곡, 합창곡, 실내악곡, 협주곡, 그리고 오페라 등 50여곡의 작품이 있다.

관련악을 위한 덧뵈기: "덧뵈기"란 탐노름이라는 말이다. 또한 "덧"이라 "탈"을 듯하는 말로서, "탈"은 얼굴의 형태이다. 탈은 물체이고 인간의 얼굴 또한 미래의 물체이다. 그러기에 탈은 인간일 수가 있다. 그 탈 속에 우리 조상의 웃음과 고마, 분노와 용기, 아울러 풍자와 해학이 담겨있고, 다양한 형태의 자유로움이 있고, 또한 가장 외면적이면서도 가장 내면적이기도 하다. 그래서 탈의 매력을 느끼게 된다.

DEOT BOE KI: A mask-dance play is called Deot Boe Ki in the Korean language. "Deot" itself means a mask which shows the countenance of a human face. The mask is a substance, and the human face is also destined to be a substance in the future. Therefore, the mask is personified as a human being. Joy and agony, the fury and courage of our ancestors were expressed in the mask as well with their satire and humor. The mask connotes a variety of freedoms by the most internal and external characteristics. That is the point of attraction in the mask.

Marilyn Shrude received degrees from Alverno College and Northwestern University, where she studied with Alan Stout and M. William Karlins. Several of Marilyn Shrude's works have been recorded for Orion, Access, and Ohio Brassworks. PASSAGE OF YEARS was commissioned and premiered in 1987 by the brilliant young conductor, Kate Tamarkin, to celebrate the 20th anniversary of the Fox Valley Symphony. As the title suggests, the piece reflects the swift movement of time with its volatile and introspective moments—time which always seems to defy our grasp. Marilyn Shrude writes: "As in many of my compositions, there is a strong concentration on timbre and its subtle manipulation; a single sound may be transformed throughout

=== Page 33 ===
the entire orchestral resource. The harmonic language is mildly atonal, and the single repeated rhythmic motive becomes incessantly driving, projecting the piece forward through three contrasting sections until its culmination on the final chord."

앤드류 임브리는 버클리에 있는 캘리포니아대학 교수이며, 그곳에서 1949년부터 가르쳐 왔다. 1921년 뉴욕대학에 입학한 그는 프린스턴대학과, 버클리대학에서 학위를 받았고, 라오 온스타인과 로저 세션에게서 작곡을 배웠다.
그의 작품은 교향곡, 협주곡, 현악4중주곡, 소나타, 합창곡, 노래 실내악곡, 오페라 등 아주 다양하다. 그는 많은 상과 연구비를 받았고, 또 많은 연주단체 (San Francisco Symphony, San Francisco Opera, Oakland Symphony, New York Philharmonic, Pro Arte Quartet), 기관 (Ford, Fromm, Koussevitzky, Naumburg), 학교 (Dartmouth, University of Wisconsin)로부터 작품 위촉을 받았다. 그는 현재 <피아노 협주곡 3번>을 작곡중이다.

드림 시퀀스는 프랭크 태프린의 위촉으로 작곡되어 1986년 6월 17일 완성되었다. 「드림 시퀀스」란 제목은 이 곡의 작곡이 완성된 후에 떠올랐다는, 이것은 꿈이 묘사되는 언어나 영화의 어떤 장면을 연상하고 있다. 이러한 장면은 일련의 이벤트들로 이루어져 있는 것이 전형적인 방법인데, 이 경우 연속되는 이벤트들은 이치에 맞지 않게 나타나지만, 어떻게해서든지 주인공의 심리상태를 설명해주는 데에 한 몫을 하게 된다. 이 제목은 이 곡의 표제로서 잘 들어맞는다고 생각하는데, 그 이유는 새들의 지저귐, 동양 민속음악의 파편, 혹은 다른 음악적 표시들이 나타나는 것에 대한 합리적인 이야기의 설명이 없기 때문이다.

제1악장은 좀 열광적으로 시작한다. 이어서 양설이 듯한 비올라의 선율이 따라 나오는데, 이 선율은 간헐적으로 처음의 베니스러운 반주를 가지고 있다. 이 아이디어의 전개가 중단되지만, 동시에 플루트에 의하여 응답되고, 곧이어 오보에와 클라리넷이 참여한다. 이렇게 하여 모든 악기가 참여하게 되어 제1부의 끝부분을 향하여 진행하게 된다. 이 악장의 중간 부분은 지금까지의 악상과는 크게 대조를 이루게 되는데, 즉 악음기를 건 현악기에 의하여 예고되어 잉글리쉬 혼이 그 특징을 이루고 있다. 이후고 피아노가 현악기에 참여하게 되고 베이스 클라리넷이 잉글리쉬 혼의 선율을 회상시켜 준다. 이어서 제1부에서 파생된 요소들이 새로운 모습과 위치에 의하여 재현된다. 동시에 이러한 본질적으로 다른 요소들이 아치형의 선율에 의하여 보다 단단히 얽어지게 된다. 이 선율선의 클라리넷은 높은 음역에서의 이점적인 부분(앞에서 피아노에 의하여 나타났음)이 재현되는 것과 일치하고 있는데, 이번에는 피콜로에 의하여 연주된다. 제1악장은 코다에 의하여 끝난다.

제2악장은 분명히 스케르포이지만, 다음과 같은 설명이 부연되어야 하겠다. 즉, 전통적인 스케르포는 빠른 3박자로 움직이며, 춤곡풍의 성질이 끊임없이 들리게 된다. 이 작품에서 빠른 3박자가 항상 존재하지만, 이는 뒤에 숨겨져 있을 뿐이다(비록 표면에 나타나는 경우가 가끔씩 생기지만).

마지막 악장은 아다지오로서, 오보에의 긴 선율에 의하여 시작하고 마친다.

Andrew Imbrie is a Professor of Music at the University of California at Berkeley, and has taught there since 1949. Born in New York in 1921, he received degrees from Princeton University and Berkeley, and studied composition with Leo Ornstein and Roger Sessions.

Among his works are symphonies, concerti, string quartets, sonatas, choral works, songs, chamber pieces, and operas. He has received numerous awards and fellowships, and has had works commissioned by professional ensembles (the San Francisco Symphony, San Francisco Opera, Oakland Symphony, New York Philharmonic, and the Pro Arte Quartet), foundations (Ford, Fromm, Koussevitzky, and Naumburg), schools (Dartmouth and the University of Wisconsin) and individuals. He is currently working on a Third Piano Concerto.

DREAM SEQUENCE was commissioned by Mr. Frank Taplin and was completed on June 17, 1986.

The title Dream Sequence occurred to me some time after I had finished writing the piece. It refers to any passage in a play or movie where a dream is portrayed. Such a scene typically comprises a series of events whose succession appears illogical, yet serves to illustrate in some way a protagonist's state of mind. The title seemed to fit the piece because there is no reasonable narrative explanation for why a particular bird-call, fragment of Oriental folk-melody, or other musical detail found its way in. These things were needed; they were part of the dream.

The first movement opens rather feverishly with a long phrase characterized by dynamic surges, unstable texture, and a quick dissolution. This is followed by a halting viola melody, supported intermittently by a low, fitful accompaniment. The development of this idea is interrupted, but at the same time answered, by the flute, soon joined by oboe and clarinet; whereupon all instruments participate in a

=== Page 34 ===
more sustained drive toward the goal of the first section. This consists of an insistent disjunct passage for the piano in its and subsequent collapse. The middle part of the movement strongly contrasts with all this: it is ushered in by muted strings, and characterized by a reflective English horn melody. Eventually the piano joins the strings and the bass clarinet recalls the English horn melody. Following this, elements derived from the first section reappear in new guises and positions. At the same time these disparate elements are more tightly woven together by means of an overarching melodic line. The climax of this line coincides with the return of the high disjunct music (previously for piano), now played by the piccolo. A coda brings the movement to a close.

The second movement is really a scherzo, but this description ought to be qualified in the following way. A traditional scherzo moves in fast triple time, and the listener is consistently aware of its dance-like quality. In this movement the quick triple meter is always present, but although sometimes in the foreground it is merely latent, owing to the tendency of the music to broaden into a kind of evanescent lyricism, or else to redivide the measure into fours or fives, etc., rather than into threes. The scherzo quality therefore derives as much from shifts of metrical focus as from an evocation of the dance. The "persona" behind the scherzo adopts changing disguises.

The last movement is an adagio, begun and ended by a long oboe melody.

Marshall Bialosky was born in Cleveland, Ohio in 1923. Since 1950, he has taught Music at the University of Chicago, State University of New York at Stony Brook, and currently at California State University, Dominguez Hills (in Los Angeles) where he was the founding Chairman of the Music and Art Departments in 1964.

His teachers of Composition have included Lionel Lowak, Luigi Dallapiccola, and Ernst Bacon. A past national Chairman of the Society of Composers, Inc., he is currently the President of the National Association of Composers, a post he has held since 1978. In 1983, he formed the Sanjo Music Company for the Publication of the own music where the bulk of his work has been in the fields of choral, vocal and chamber music.

TWO MOVEMENTS FOR STRING QUARTET AND PIANO was originally commissioned in 1957 by the Berkshire Music Center (Tanglewood) where it was awarded the Wechslar Prize given to outstanding alumni. The first movement is a kind of "permuted passacaglia" where, instead of returning to the beginning of the recurring theme, each variation begins one measure further on; first with the second measure, then the third, and so on. When the end of the theme is reached, the process is reversed until the music works itself back to the opening solo theme which this time is heard as a canon in the string quartet while the piano "heralds" the theme of the second movement. The second movement is a highly developed sonata-form type of piece which, in a climactic moment towards the end, recalls the pitch pattern of the first movement's

=== Page 35 ===
theme. The entire piece is based on a twelve-note row which is the same backwards as it is forwards, although, of course, at a different transposition.

그레고리 코르치마: 1947년생인 그레고리 코르치마는 작곡과 피아노전공으로 레닌그라드 콘서바토리를 졸업했다. 그는 레닌그라드 콘서바토리에서 피아노부문 재판 수상자이며 실내악단에서 피아노와 하프시코드 연주자로 20년 동안 일해 왔다. 현재 코르치마는 <Solests of Leningrad> 실내악단의 단원이다.
그는 이 악단과 함께 소련 전역과 미국, 스페인, 핀란드, 유고슬라비아, 동독, 폴란드등에 연주여행을 했다.
코르치마는 많은 장르의 음악을 작곡했다. 그의 작품은 오페라, 교향곡, 심포니에타, 여러가지 악기를 위한 협주곡들, 칸타타, 다양한 악기배합의 실내악 작품들, 어린이를 위한 음악등 다채롭다. 그의 작품은 출판되고 음반으로 제작되어 널리 보급되어 있으며, 그는 <Leningrad Musical Spring Festival>에 자주 참가한다.
그레고리 코르치마는 소련 작곡가협회의 레닌그라드 지부장인 동시에 미-소 음악교류센터의 소련측 회장직도 맡고 있다.

CONCERTO-DIPTYCH(비올라[첼로], 타악기 오케스트라, 첼레스타, 하프) (1981): 작곡자의 주된 아이디어는 “인간혼(人間魂)의 소리”를 “주변세계의 소리”와 대비시키는 것 외에도, 감정상태와 음악적 수단과의 대비성을 재생시켜 보는 것이다. 이 곡의 제1부 (Notturno)는 휴식과 신비의 전형적인 상태를 가진 “밤의 음악”이다. 독주자들의 선율 프레이즈들은 마치 신비로운 소리들(큰 음향과 바스라거리는 음향 등)에 싸여진 것처럼 되어 있는데, 이 신비로운 소리들은 음고를 가진 금속악기들을 가진 타악기 오케스트라에 의하여 만들어진다.
제2부 (Perpetuum mobile)는 토타카로서, 서로 대조적인 정열적인 악장들과 불안하고 신경질적인 리듬, 그리고 앞의 Notturno 악장에서의 경직된 분위기와는 반작용을 하는 오스티나토 원리등을 가지고 있다. 여기에서는 불안, 공포, 그리고 인생생활에서의 노력 등에 대한 감정을 조화한 “과민한” 음향을 가진 일반의 악기들에 의하여 재생되고 있다. 즉, 비올라의 불안한 소리가 들어와서 끊임없이 다른 악기들과 대화를 가지게 되는데, 작품의 마지막 부분에 가서야 비로소 개화(開花)와 조화의 상태에 도달하게 된다. 이 곡에서는 서로 결합된 주제적 소재가 작품 전체를 통하여 변화하면서 내부세계와 외부세계를 결합시 키는 감각을 촉진시켜주고 있다. 또한, 비올라와 이를 반주하는 악기들에 의한 표현적인 기교와 색채적인 가능성들이 이 작품 전체에 걸쳐서 폭넓게 사용되고 있다.
이 곡의 조연은 서독의 Cologne에서 있었다. 그리고 Melodiya에 의하여 취입되었으며, “Sovetsky Compozitor” 출판사에 의하여 출판되었다.

Gregory Korchmar graduated from the Leningrad Conservatory with degrees in Composition and Piano. He is a laureate of the all-Russian competition among pianists, and worked for twenty years as pianist and harpsichordist with a chamber orchestra. At present Korchmar is member of the chamber ensemble Soloists of Leningrad. He has toured with this group throughout the Soviet Union and the U.S., Sweden, Finland, Yugoslavia, East Germany, and Poland.
Mr. Korchmar has composed in many different genres: his output includes operas, symphonies, sinfoniettas, concertos for a variety of instruments, cantatas, chamber works for different ensembles and solo instruments, and music for children. His works have been widely published and recorded, and he has been a frequent participant in the Leningrad Musical Spring Festival.
Gregory Korchmar serves as Secretary of the Leningrad branch of the Board of the Union of Composers of the USSR, and is the President of the Soviet Union Branch of the Center for Soviet-American Musical Exchange.

CONCERTO-DIPTYCH for viola (cello), percussion orchestra, celesta and harp(1981) was set for an original cast of performers and consists of two parts without interval—Notturno and Perpetuum Mobile. The composer’s principal idea is to reproduce contrasting emotional states with musical means, as well as to contrast the voice of man’s soul with that of the surrounding world. The first part of the composition (Notturno) is “night music” with typical states of rest and mystery. The melodic phrases of the soloist are as if cloaked with mystic peals and rustles, made by the percussion orchestra with pitched metal instruments.
The second part (Perpetuum mobile) is a toccata with contrasting energetic movements, uneasy nervous rhythms and the use of ostinato principles which counteract the static atmosphere of the notturno. The sensation of anxiety, alarm and effort of today’s life is reproduced with the group of instruments with dry “prickly” sonorousness. The anxious voice of the viola enters into constant dialogue with different instruments, and only at the end of the composition does the state of enlightenment and harmony come. United thematic material, changing through the whole composition,

=== Page 36 ===
promotes the sensation of unity of the internal and the external world. The expressive mastery and coloring possibilities of the viola and the accompanying instruments are widely used in the composition.

The premiere of the Concerto-Diptych took place in Cologne, West Germany. The composition was recorded by Melodiya and is published by the publishing house "Sovetsky Compozitor."

김정길 (金正佶)은 15세 때부터 트럼펫을 공부했으며, 이듬해부터 작곡공부를 시작하였다. 계명대학교 재학 시절 그는 전액장학금을 받으며 공부했으며, 졸업 후 대구에서 8년간 음악교사로 일한 후, 1976년 계명대학교 대학원을 졸업하였다. 또한 그는 캘리포니아 주립대학교(로스앤젤레스)에서 김병곤 박사로부터 작곡을 배우기도 하였다.

그의 작품들은 창악회와 创友會, 패시픽현대음악센터 (PCMC), 국제음악교육협회 (ISME)등에 의한 많은 연주회에서 발표되었다. 이 외에도 대한민국 정부로부터 위촉받은 관련악곡「神話」, 계명실내악단에 의하여 위촉받은 「콜라츠」등을 통하여서도 현란한 작품활동을 하고 있다. 현재 계명대학교 부교수로 재직중이며, 创友會의 회장직과 ISME의 대구지부장을 맡고 있다.

바이올린과 비아노를 위한 세 개의 노래: 나는 어렸을 때에 슬픈 소설을 읽는 것이 커다란 즐거움이었다. 나는 이들 소설에 대단히 심취했으며, 내 마음이 움직이지 않을 수 없었다. 나는 특히 나이체, 고피, 보리스 파스테르나크의 비극에 감명을 받았다.

이 곡은 이러한 작품들에서의 나의 반응을 표현해주고 있다. 나는 비극이 우리들에게는 나이와 국적을 초월한, 누구의 마음 속에서나 존재할 수 있는 영원한 것이라 생각한다.

Jeong-Gil Kim, born in Daegu, Korea in 1941, began his musical study with the trumpet at the age of fifteen and his studies in composition one year later. Mr. Kim attended Keimyung University as a full scholarship student. After earning his Bachelor of Music degree, he was employed as a music teacher in Daegu for eight years. In 1970, he entered the graduate school at Keimyung University and received a Master of Music degree with the highest distinction in 1976. He also studied composition with Dr. Byoungkon Kim at California State University, Los Angeles.

Jeong-Gil Kim's works have been performed at many concerts in Korea. He is active in the Asian Composers League and the two professional composer's organizations—Chang Ack and Chang Woo—in Seoul and Daegu, respectively, Pacific Contemporary Music Center, and the International Society for Music Education (ISME). In addition to these professional activities, Mr. Kim has had many commissions, including the recent orchestral work, Myth, commissioned by the Korean government, and a work for string orchestra, Collage, commissioned by Keimyung Chamber Orchestra.

Currently, Mr. Kim is an associate professor at Keimyung University and president of Chang Woo Hoe and the Daegu branch of ISME.

THREE SONGS FOR VIOLIN AND PIANO: In my childhood, it was a great pleasure for me to read tragic fiction. My heart was always absorbed in these books and quite often I could not help but explore my emotional response. I was especially impressed by reading the tragedies of Nietzsche, Goethe and Boris Pasternak.

Three Songs for Violin and Piano represent my emotional reaction to these works. My feeling is that tragedy is the one and eternal condition for us, so it exists equally in our heart, beyond the ages and the world.

데이빗 오커: 작곡가겸 클라리넷 연주자인 데이빗 오커는 미국 아이오아주에서 성장하여 Carleton College와 California Institute of the Arts에서 공부했다. 그는 로스앤젤레스 지역의 창작음악을 촉진시키기 위한 모임이었던 Independent Composer's Association의 발기위원이며 후에는 회장도 역임했다. 1986년에는 실내악단 <XTET>의 설립 회원이었다.

David Ocker: Composer/clarinetist David Ocker grew up in Iowa and attended Carleton College and the California Institute of the Arts. Mr. Ocker was a founding member and later President of the Independent Composer's Association which continues to produce new Music in Los Angeles. In 1986 he was a founding member of XTET, a chamber ensemble.

Ocker's compositions include solo, chamber, orchestral, and tape music. His works include a solo bass clarinet piece derived from a Brahms symphony, a solo bass piece in which the performer both sings and plays, a set of musical limericks, a five-hour tape environment, and a computer program to generate music from fractals. His music has been performed by the California E.A.R. Unit at the Monday Evening Concerts and the Cal-Arts Music Festival.

Besides his performances with XTET, David Ocker has given solo clarinet recitals, featuring performances of new music, since 1980. In 1983, Ocker was soloist with the London Symphony Orchestra in London in the world premiere of Mo'n Herb's Vacation, a work for clarinet and orchestra by Frank Zappa. A recording of the work is available on Zappa's Barking Pumpkin label.

Mr. Ocker is active as a music calligrapher, preparing new music of other composers for performance and publication. Composers with whom he has worked closely on major projects include Frank Zappa, John Adams and William Kraft. Ocker was Zappa's Synclavier Programmer and worked on such unknown monuments as the Francesco Zappa album and the infamous "While You Were Art" incident. Ocker now lives in Los Angeles, California, where he works late into the night.

PRIDE AND FOOLISHNESS: Five often un-asked questions about Pride and Foolishness:

Q: Why did you call your piece Pride and Foolishness?
A: I named it after the two most important qualities a composer can have while writing music. if you don't try to make the work as well-crafted as your previous musical experience will allow, you can't feel pride in it. If you don't take chances and thus risk appearing foolish, you and your music won't grow and change.

Q: Why did you write Pride and Foolishness?
A: I don't Know. It won't have much effect in the GNP, nor will it solve the problems of homelessness, illiteracy or television. I guess it kept me off the streets.

Q: Are there formal musical structures in Pride and Foolishness which you have developed in previous pieces?
A: Yes

Q: What could someone listen for during a performance of Pride and Foolishness?
A: There's a melody which is supposed to be quite prominent, and two supporting lines: continuous running notes which move from instrument to instrument, and a punctuating octave figure. These three elements change their overall relationships about half way through the piece.

=== Page 38 ===
There are also gradual modulations and tempo changes.

Steven Stucky:
1949년생인 스티븐 스틱키는 미국 여러 지역의 교향악단들로부터 작품 위촉을 받았으며 그의 작품은 아트란타, 보스턴, 덴버, 디트로이트, 샌프란시스코 등지의 교향악단에 의해 연주되었다. 또한 아나하이 <Boston Musica Viva>, <New York New Music Ensemble>, <Pennsylvania Quintet>, <Pittsburgh New Music Ensemble>등 일류 실내악단도 그에게 작품을 위촉했다. 그는 요즈음 카네기홀 백주년을 기념하기 위한 교향악을 쓰고 있는데, 이 곡은 카네기재단과 로스엔젤레스 필하모닉이 공동 위촉한 것으로 1990년 9월의 초연을 앞두고 있다.

스티크는 활동적인 지휘자이며, 강연자이고, 또 저술가이다. 폴란드의 작곡가 룰토슬라브스키에 관한 저서 <Lutoslawski and His Music> (1981년 출간) 그는 <ASCAP Deems Taylor Award>를 수상했다. 그는 1986-87년에 <Guggenheim Fellowship>을 받았으며 그의 <Concerto for Orchestra>는 1989년 뮤리처상 음악에 오르기도 했다. 베일러대학과 코넬대학을 졸업한 스틱키는 로스엔젤레스 필하모닉의 상임 작곡가가 되었다.

1988년 9월 스틱키는<Meet the Composer, Inc.>의 <Orchestral Residencies Program>의 후원으로, 또한 브렌더재단과 리더스 다이제스트/라이더 워너스 기금을 받아 로스엔젤레스 필하모닉의 상임 작곡가가 되었다.

소리와 빛(Sound and Light):
일종의 소리로서 유직히 혹은 유명한 빛임을 찾는 관광객들 위하여 작곡되었음은 오케스트라를 위한 연예물로서, 주제는 "색채"와 "밝은 외관", 그리고 "희미한 백색"과 상연되는 것이다. 이 음악에서 나는, 규칙적인 박자와 빈번히는 리듬에 의하여 그 사용이 가능한 활기와 직접성을 되찾는 데에 주력하였다. 즉, 근대 사회조직에서는 금지되었으나, 근래에 들어서 존 아담스, 스티브 라이히 등의 현대작품들에서 복구된 그러한 박자와 리듬을 뜻한다. 잔란한 9분동안의 시간을 통하여 이 곡은 거의 모두 짧고, 분주한 오스티나토 음형들로 채워져 있다. 이러한 시도에서의 나의 의도는 미니멀리즘의 리듬적 활력을 얻는 데에 있는데, 그러나 이러한 음악에 흔히 따라다니는 너무 단순화되어버린 화성어법은 여기에 주어지지 않았다.

놀랍게도 이 음악에서의 소재는 대충 19세기의 소나타 형식의 형태로 보이게 되었다. 즉, 여기에서 우리는 서주부, 제1주제(3회음의 분산화음에 기초를 둠), 제2주제(블루트 독주로 시작함), 그리고 종결주제 (두개의 피아노에 의하여 나타남)등 들을 수 있다. 발전부에 해당되는 부분에서는 지금까지의 소재들이 새로운 방법으로 재결합되어 나타나며, 재현부에서는 제1, 2주제가 모두 거의 본래의 모습으로 회상된다(제2주제는 사실상 제시부의 것이 그대로 반복되고 있다).

코다에 들어가서는 두번째 놀라운 일이 생긴다. 즉, 여기에서 마치 전혀 상이한, 또다른 음악이 빛나는 외관의 뒷면에 숨어있었던 것처럼, 현악기들이 이제는 동연히 나누어져 소리와 밝게 의한 외부의 소리를 뚫고 새롭고, 보다 정열적이며, 또한 보다 "엄숙한"음향을 내게 된다.

볼터모어 심포니 오케스트라에 의하여 위촉된 이 곡은 1988년 6월-12월 사이에 이타카(뉴욕주), 로스엔젤레스, 그리고 사라토가 스프링스(뉴욕주)등지에서 작곡되었다. 초연은 데이빗 진만의 지휘로 1989년 5월 18일 볼터모어에서 있었다.

Steven Stucky, born in 1949, has received commissions from orchestras across the United States, and his works have been performed by orchestras in Atlanta, Boston, Denver, Detroit and San Francisco. Leading chamber ensembles have also commissioned new works, among them the Boston Musica Viva, the New York New Music Ensemble, the Pennsylvania Quintet, and the Pittsburgh New Music Ensemble. Among his current projects is a new orchestral work commemorating the centennial season of Carnegie Hall, jointly commissioned by Carnegie and the Los Angeles Philharmonic for a September 1990 premiere.

Mr. Stucky is also an active conductor, lecturer, and writer. His 1981 book on the important Polish composer Witold Lutoslawski, Lutoslawski and His Music, won the ASCAP Deems Taylor Award for excellence in writing about music. He held a Guggenheim Fellowship in 1986-87, and his Concerto for Orchestra was a finalist for the 1986 Pulitzer Prize. A graduate of Baylor and Cornell Universities, Mr. Stucky has taught at Lawrence, has been a Visiting Fellow of the Royal Academy of Music in London, and since 1980, has been on the faculty of Cornell University.

In September 1988 Mr. Stucky became Composer-in-Residence of the Los Angeles Philharmonic, under the auspices of the Orchestral Residencies Program administered by Meet the Composer, Inc., with major funding from the Rockefeller Foundation and the Reader's Digest/Lila Wallace Fund.

Son et lumiere ("Sound and Light," a kind of show staged for tourists at historic sites or famous buildings) is an orchestral entertainment whose subject is the play of col-

=== Page 39 ===
ors, bright surfaces, and shimmery textures. I have tried in this music to recapture the elan and immediacy that regular meters and repetitive rhythms make possible—something forbidden during the modernist regime but recently restored in the postmodern work of composers like John Adams, Steve Reich, and others. Throughout its brief nine-minute span, the piece is built almost exclusively of short, busy ostinato figures—my attempt, I suppose, to achieve the rhythmic vitality of minimalism, but without giving in to the over-simple harmonic language that usually comes with it.

Surprisingly, the musical materials seemed determined to shape themselves into an approximation of nineteenth-century sonata form. We hear an introduction, a first theme (Based on triadic broken chords), a second theme (beginning with the flute solo), and a closing theme (led by two piccolos). In a sort of development section, these materials are recombined in new ways, and in a recapitulation, both the first and second themes are recalled more or less intact (part of the second is actually repeated quite literally). Then, in the coda a second surprise: As if another, different music has been lurking all the while behind the shiny surface, the strings now unexpectedly split off from the rest of the orchestra to assert a new, more passionate, more “serious” voice, transcending the external show of sound and light.

Son et lumiere, commissioned by the Baltimore Symphony Orchestra, was composed between June and December 1988 in Ithaca (N.Y.), in Los Angeles, and at the artists’ colony Yaddo, in Saratoga Springs (N.Y.). David Zinman conducted the first performance in Baltimore on 18 May 1989.

INTERPLAY: The title tells much about the piece: there are three ideas which form the basis for the ensuing interplay, or variations. The term "ideas" is used rather than "themes," because it is the character of each of these ideas, not the actual pitch and rhythmic content that, for the most part, is exploited throughout the piece.

The three ideas are presented in an introductory section. The first idea is stated by way of a cello cadenza, second by flutes, and then, later, strings. My choice of instruments here was shaped in part by my admiration for the playing of the Los Angeles Philharmonic's principal cellist, Ronald Leonard, and for the orchestra's flutists.

While the second idea is still being played, the third enters. It consists simply of four parallel thirds played by an ensemble of three percussionists on vibraphone, orchestra bells and crotales. The exposition of three percussionists on vibraphone, orchestra bells and crotales. The exposition of these ideas concludes with the timpani fragmenting the second idea. The interplay of all this begins immediately thereafter.

Ideas one and two are never again stated completely, but rather, they are fragmented, and it is the elements resulting from that fragmentation which are exploited and varied.

The interplay consists not only of the interaction of the elements themselves, but also in the way they are thrown about the orchestra. The word "play" within the title is descriptive of the character of the piece itself.

Interplay was commissioned by the Los Angeles Philharmonic for the occasion of the 80th birthday of Dorothy Chandler, and received its premiere on November 1, 1984, in the Dorothy Chandler Pavilion with Simon Rattle conducting.

김용진 (金容振) 은 서울대 음대, 동 대학원, 미국 메하탄 음악학교, 동 일리노이 주립대학교 대학원에서 수학했으며, 현재 서울대학교 음악대학 교수로 재직 중이다. 그의 작품은 국내외 여러 음악제를 위시하여 미국 동남아 등지의 각종 음악제에서 연주되었으며, 사회적인 활동으로는 창악회 회장(76-86)을 역임한 것을 비롯하여, 아시아작곡가연맹 부회장, 국제현대음악협회 회원 등으로 활동중이며, 지난 84-85년에는 미국 펜실베니아대학교 (University of Pennsylvania)객원교수를 역임하였다.

대금과 현악합주를 위한 소협주곡은 서울 바르크합주단의 위촉작품으로 1983년 봄에 완성되어 그 해 10월에 동 협주단에 의하여 초연된 곡이다. 이 작품은 비교적 넓은 음역과 풍부한 음량, 악장표현에 있어서의 자유로움, 또한 지취나 평취에 있어서의 무드리고 아름다운 음색, 역취에서의 강쾌한 갈대청의 음을 지닌 대금과, 폭넓은 표현력을 지닌 서양의 현악기의 협주와의 조화의 가능성을 모색한, 이질적인 두 개의 악기군과의 음합을 시도한 작품이다. 이 곡은 비교적 단순한 음구조로 되어 있으며, 종적인 조화와 선적인 대화를 통한 소협주곡의 형태로 이루어져 있다.

CONCERTINO FOR TAEGUM AND STRING ENSEMBLE was written in 1983 commissioned by the Korean Chamber Ensemble. This music, consisting of a single movement, has a simple tone structure and a mood of Oriental atmosphere. The tones are applied vertically and linearly with contrasting dynamics, spacing, tone color, density and so on. This piece pursues the possibilities of expressing beauty in an Oriental idiom combining one of the famous Korean traditional woodwind instruments, the Taegum, and Western string instruments.

Donald Erb was born in Youngstown, Ohio in 1927. His orchestral music has been played by literally every major orchestra in the United States and many in Europe and Australia as well. He has had major commissions from the

His early experience as a professional jazz trumpeter has led to a number of compositions in that medium, one for jazz great Jim Hall.

PRISMATIC VARIATIONS was completed on August 18, 1983. It was written on commission of Leonard Slatkin, Music Director of the St. Louis Symphony, who with his orchestra gave the first performance of the work on January 28, 1984. It has since been performed by the New York Philharmonic, the Chicago Symphony, the Festival of the Americas Orchestra, and others.

Mr. Erb writes: "Composers are often surprised by the qualities their music presents to the public, but this work will, I think, have a couple of qualities that will be exemplified by the title I have chosen. One thing I have tried to achieve in this piece is to fill the hall with bright, transparent sound. This is accomplished by the orchestra, but it is also enhanced by participants in the audience who are called upon to play, separately or in combination, such instruments as harmonicas, soda bottles and telephone bells. The other quality that this piece should have has to do with the fact that much of the music is repeated during the course of the work, but is, altered by being radically reorchestrated for each successive appearance. In other words, some of the variations are simply changes in orchestration and not changes in the shape of the theme—or that of the preceeding variation. This gives the work a quality similar in some ways to a rondo as much as to a theme and variations."

The score calls for two flutes and piccolo, two oboes and English horn, two clarinets and bass clarinet, two bassoons and contrabassoon, four horns, three trumpets, three trombones, tuba, timpani, a large percussion ensemble, three harmonicas, slide whistle, piano, electric piano, electric organ, harp, strings and approximately eighty young people in the audience playing harmonicas, soda bottles, stemmed glasses and telephone bells.

카렐 후사: 퓨리처상 수상자인 카렐 후사는 국제적으로 명성이 높은 작곡가겸 지휘자이다. 그는 1945년 이후 줄곧 코넬 대학에서 가르쳐 왔으며, 현재는 Kappa Alpha Professor직을 맡고 있다. 그는 1921년 8월 7일 체코슬로바키아의 프라하에서 태어났으나 1959년 미국 국민이 되었다. 그는 <Prague Conservatory and Academy of Music>을 졸업한 후 도브하악 파리의 <National Conservatory and Ecole Normale de Musique>에서 디플롬을 받았다. 그는 아티 오베거, 나디아 블랑케, 아로슬라브 렛키, 그리고 지휘자 안드레 클뤼네로부터 음악 수업을 받았다.

Karel Husa, Pulitzer Prize winner in Music, is an internationally known composer and conductor and the Kappa Alpha professor at Cornell University, where he has taught since 1945. An American citizen since 1959, Husa was born in Prague, Czechoslovakia on August 7, 1921. After completing studies at the Prague Conservatory and Academy of Music, he went to Paris, France Where he received diplomas from the National Conservatory and Ecole de Musique. Among his teachers were Arthur Honegger, Nadia Boulanger, Jaroslav Ridky and conductor Andre Cluytens.

In 1974, Mr. Husa was elected Associate Member of the Royal Belgian Academy of Arts and Sciences; he has also received honorary Doctor of Music degrees from Coe College, the Cleveland Institute of Music, and Ithaca College. He has been the recipient of many awards, fellowships, and commissions, including a Guggenheim Fellowship, awards from the American Academy and Institute of Arts and Letters, UNESCO, and the National Endowment for the Arts awards, Koussevitzky Foundation Commission, the Czech Academy for the Arts and Sciences Prize, and the Lili Boulanger Award.

His 3rd String Quartet received the 1969 Pulitzer Prize, and, With over 7000 performances, his Music for Prague 1968 has become part of the modern repertory. His Concerto for Wind Ensemble received the first Sudler International Prize. Among recent works the Concerto for Orchestra was commissioned by the New York Philharmonic and Zubin Mehta and premiered in 1986, and the Concerto for Trumpet was commissioned by the Chicago Symphony and Sir Georg Solti, who premiered it with soloist Adolph Herseth in Chicago. Other recent works include the Concerto for Organ (1987) and Concerto for Violoncello(1988), premiered by Lynn Harrell.

Recordings of Husa's music have been issued by CBS Masterworks, Vox, Everest, Louisville, CRI and others.

MUSIC FOR PRAGUE 1986 was first performed in its orchestral version on January 31, 1970, with the composer conducting the Munich Philharmonic Orchestra. The premiere of the original version for concert band took Place in Washington, D. C. on January 31, 1989, with Dr. Kenneth Snapp conducting the Ithaca College Concert Band in concert for the Music Educator's National Conference.

The work was commissioned by the Ithaca Band and composed during the summer and fall of 1968 for the capital city of Czechoslovakia. Since then, the work has been per-

=== Page 44 ===
formed by virtually every major American orchestra, as well as by university and community ensembles. In Asia, the Hong Kong Philharmonic and Singapore Symphony have played the work under the composer's baton.

Three main ideas bind the composition together. The first and most important is an old Hussite war song from the 15th century, "Ye Warriors of God and His Law", a symbol of resistance and hope for hundreds of years, whenever fate lay heavy on the Czech nation. It has been utilized by many Czech composers, including Smetana in "My country." The beginning of this religious song is announced very softly in the first movement by the timpani and concludes in a strong unison (Chorale). The song is never used in its entirety.

The second idea is the sound of bells throughout: Prague, named also the city of "Hundreds of Towers," has used its magnificently sounding church bells as calls of distress as well as of victory.

The last idea is a motive of three chords first appearing very softly under the piccolo solo at the beginning of the piece, in flutes, clarinets, and horns. Later it reappears at extremely strong dynamic levels, for example, in the middle of the Aria.

Different techniques of composing as well as orchestration have been used in Music for Prague 1968 and some new sounds explored, such as the percussion section in the Interlude, and at the ending of the work. Much symbolism also appears: in addition to the distress calls in the first movement (Fanfares), the unbroken hope of the Hussite song, sound of bells, or the tragedy (Aria), there is also the bird call at the beginning (piccolo solo), symbol of the liberty which the City of Prague has seen only for moments during its thousand years of existence.

캘리포니아 <이어-유닛> 연주단: 캘리포니아<이어-유닛> 연주단은 현대음악의 창작, 연주활동을 촉진시키기 위해 설립된 9인조 연주단이다. <이어-유닛>은 1981년 로스엔젤레스에 사는 작곡가와 연주가들에 의해 창립되었는데, 그 취지는 로스엔젤레스시에 처음으로 자치적으로 운영되는 현대음악 전문 실내악단을 만들어 보자는 것이었다.

발족한지 7년만에 <이어-유닛>은 미국에서 가장 뛰어난 실내악단 중의 하나로 각광받게 되었다. <이어-유닛>은 "캘 아츠(California Institute of the Arts) 현대음악제", "월요 음악회", "나-카메라회"등에 정기적으로 출연함으로써 남가주지방에 현대음악을 촉진시키는 큰 힘이 되었다. 또한 로스엔젤레스의 올림피 예술제와 축제, 뉴뮤직 아메리카등에도 출연하였다.

로스엔젤레스 이외의 지방에서도 <이어-유닛>은 국내외 국제적으로 커다란 영향력을 발휘하여 "네덜란드 음악제", "미국무용제", "오하이오 음악제", 파리의 "미국센터", "워커 예술센터", "하바드-프롬 시리즈", 등에서 활약하였으며 이 연주단의 뉴욕 데뷔 무대였던 "아메리칸 인스트루시리즈"에서는 대단한 갈채를 받은 바 있다.

특별은 레퍼토리로 유명한 <이어-유닛>은 연주하기 어려운 음악작품들로부터 극음악에 이르기까지 다양한 작품을 소화해 내고, 때로는 이 단체내의 수상경력 있는 작곡가들 연주기들의 작품이 무대에 오르기도 한다. 연주단의 기본적 악기 구성은 플루트, 클라리넷, 건반악기, 타악기, 바이올린, 첼로등으로 이루어져 있으며, 경우에 따라 여기에 성악, 팬 파이프등의 악기, 또는 기계나 전자매체가 참가되기도 한다. 그들이 연주한 득이한 작품으로서는 팬 파이프, 증기, 드럼, 피아노, 전자 피아노, 전자 베이스를 위한 <Hoketus>, 컴퓨터를 이용한 생연주 전자음악인 <The Key to Songs>, 확장된 성악음악인 <Stimmung> 등이 있다.

설립 당시부터<이어-유닛>은 많은 작곡가들과 긴밀한 유대관계를 가졌으며. 그들은 헨리 브란트, 엘 브라운, 빈코 글로보카, 조안 라 바바라, 스티븐 모스크, 로버트 로드리게스, 모턴, 서바토너등과 함께 연주했으며, 존 아담스, 루이 안드리센, 머니타 마쿠스, 마우리치오 카셀, 밀튼 베넷, 엘리오 카티, 존 케이지, 모턴 펠드만, 멜 파웰, 피터 맥스웰 데이비스등이 이 악단을 이끌어 왔다.
<이어-유닛>은 로스엔젤레스 미술관, 캘리포니아 주립대학의 상주 연주단이며 특히 미술관의<Bing Theatre>에서는 자체의 연주회 시리즈를 맡고 있다. 현재<이어-유닛>은 <Western States Performing Arts Tour>와 <California Arts Council Touring Programs>등의 연주여행 활동 중이며 <Chamber Music America>, <Fromm Foundation>, <National Endowment for the Arts>등의 단체로부터 재정 지원을 받았다.

California E.A.R. Unit
The California E.A.R. Unit is a nine-member ensemble dedicated to the creation, performance, and promotion of the music of our time. The E.A.R. Unit was founded in March 1981 by a group of Los Angeles performers and composers with the goal of developing the first full-time, communally-directed repertory ensemble for new music in Los Angeles. In the seven years since its inception, the E.A.R. Unit has become recognized as one of the most important new music ensembles in the country. It is a highly visible force for contemporary music in Southern California as a result of regular appearances on the Cal-Arts Contemporary Music Festival, Monday Evening Concerts, and the Da Camera Society Series; the E.A. R. Unit has also performed at the Olympic Arts Festival, the Los Angeles Festival, and New Music America.

Outside of Los Angeles the E.A.R. unit has made a dramatic impact on the national and international scene with performances at the Holland Festival, the American Dance Festival, the Ojai Festival, the American Center in Paris, the Walker Art Center, the Harvard/Fromm Series, and the American Inroads Series in the Unit's critically-acclaimed New York debut.

Famous for its versatility, the E.A.R. Unit's repertoire ranges from the most demanding works for the concert hall to music and theater, often featuring works by the ensemble's award-winning composer/performers. The Unit combines a basic instrumentation of flute, clarinet, keyboards, percussion, violin and cello with unusual doublings including voice, panpipes, plants and electronic media. Their extensive repertoire list includes "Hoketus" for panpipes, congas, piano, electric keyboards, and electric basses; "The Key to Songs" with computer-assisted live electronics; and "Stimmung" for amplified voices.

From the outset, the E.A.R. unit has worked closely with composers in the preparation of their music. The ensemble

=== Page 46 ===
has performed with Henry Brant, Earle Brown, Vinko Globokar, Joan La Barbara, Stephen Mosko, Robert Rodriguez and Morton Subotnick; and they have been coached by John Adams, Louis Andriessen, Bunita Marcus, Mauricio Kagel, Milton Babbitt, Elliot Carter, John Cage, Morton Feldman, Mel Powell, and Sir Peter Maxwell-Davies.

The E.A.R. Unit has recorded for Nonesuch, Crystal, and New Albion Records. Many of the ensemble's concerts are heard on American and National Public Radio, and E.A.R. Unit broadcasts of American works have been chosen for the International Rostrum of Composers. The E.A.R. Unit has also been featured in video projects, including a documentary of music by West Coast composers produced by the British Broadcasting Corporation.

The E.A.R. Unit is Ensemble-in-Residence at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art, where it presents its own concert series at the Bing Theatre, and at California State University, Los Angeles. The E.A.R. Unit is currently on the rosters of the Western States Performing Arts Tour and the California Arts Council Touring Programs, and has received grants from Chamber Music America, the Fromm Foundation, and the National Endowment for the Arts.

Paul Van Ness is Professor in Piano and Chairman of the Keyboard Program at California State University, Los Angeles. He is a graduate of the Eastman School of Music in Rochester, New York, where he studied with Frank Glazer and Eugene List. As a recipient of a German Academic Exchange Grant, Mr. Van Ness studied further at the Hochschule fur Musik in Munich, West Germany.

In addition to teaching, Van Ness is an active performer and lecturer. He has appeared as soloist and chamber musician in Europe as well as throughout much of the United States and Canada. Mr. Van Ness toured Taiwan, Republic of China, where he played in all musical centers. In 1986, the List-Glenn Institute was formed by Mr. Van Ness as a memorial to the great American pianist, Eugene List, and his wife, the renowned violinist, Carroll Glenn. The Institute is dedicated to enhancing international contact and understanding through the study and performance of music for piano and strings.

Daegu Symphony Orchestra
The Daegu Symphony Orchestra was founded in November 1964, and has since performed 400 periodical and special concerts. During the past 25 years, it has provided the audience with and understanding of concert symphonic repertoire in the Daegu area as well as promoting provincial art activities under different names such as the Daegu String Orchestra, Daegu Symphony and the Daegu Broadcasting Symphony.

Its concerts are held under the baton of Mr. Soo-il Kang, who received Bachelor's and Master's degrees from Michigan State University, and has been the Associate Conductor of the Michigan State Symphony since 1987. Mr Kang works as the Conductor-in-residence for the Daegu Symphony Orchestra as well as the Keimyung University Symphony.

서울시립교향악단은 42년의 가장 긴 역사와 전통을 자랑하는 한국 교향악사의 선증인이다.
1974년 이래 현재까지 줄곧 서울시립교향악단을 이끌고 있는 음악감독이자 상임지휘자인 정재동씨의 지휘봉아래 최정상의 연주력을 인정받는 전문연주단체로서의 눈부신 발전을 이룩한 서울시향은 1990년 5월 16일 현재 422회 를 맞는 정기 연주회를 비롯하여 구민회관 방문연주, 대학순회연주 등의 수많은 대시민 봉사연주와 특별연주회를 통하여 공공음악단체로서의 모범적인 연주활동을 펴고 있으며 청소년음악회, 토요음악회, 팝스콘서트와 같은 신선한 기획연주로 음악인구 저변확대를 위해 노력해오고 있다.
연주활동 이외에도 서울시향은 소년소녀 현주회, 청소년 오디션, 지휘연수원등 일련의 프로그램을 마련, 자라나는 음악도들에게 전문음악인으로서의 등용의 기회를 제공하는 한편 지휘자 교육이 전무한 국내상황에서 신진 지휘자를 배출하는 유일한 음악교육기관으로서의 역할을 해하는 등, 우리 음악계 발전에 이바지 해오고 있다. 또한, 대외적으로는, 일제기 1965년 일본순회연주를 필두로하여 77년 동남아연주, 82·86년도 미국 동·서부순회연주, 88년도 유럽6개국 13개도시 순회연주까지 모두 5차례 해외순회연주를 통해 한국을 대표하는 최정상 교향악단으로서의 명성을 아낌없이 발휘하여 연주때마다 격찬을 받았으며, 유럽 연주지에는 음악의 본고장인 현지의 저명한 주요일간지들로부터 유럽 입금악단에 버금가는 교향악단이라는 찬사를 받는 등, 세계정상급 교향악단의 대열에 당당히 함께 서게 되었음을 확인한 바 있다.
서울시향은 음반제작에도 관심을 기울여 안익태씨의 코리안 환타지를 녹음, 출판한데 이어 1989년에는 국내최초로 컴팩트디스크를 출판하여 음반분야에서도 국내선두를 달리고 있다.
서울시향은 앞으로 현대음악작품도 최대한 수용, 홀륭한 국내외 작품들을 소개할 계획이며 지방순회연주도 정기적으로 가정예정이다.

Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra
During the Japanese occupation of Korea (1919–1945), Korean cultural activities across all social strata were oppressed. With the liberation of Korea in 1945 came a great rejuvenation of the undying Korean spirit. Cultural activities flourished again, and music was no exception. The Association of Korean Symphonies was founded on

=== Page 50 ===
September 15, 1945, and the Korean Symphony Orchestra (KSO) was born, predecessor of today's Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra (SPO). In October of 1945, the KSO gave its first concert under the baton of Maestro Chung-Shik Kye at the Sudo Theatre in Seoul. After conducting 26 KSO concerts over the next two years, Maestro Kye stepped down and Weon-Shik Yim was invited to assume leadership. The orchestra soon disbanded, however, for lack of funds.

After a silence lasting several months, the Seoul Symphony Orchestra (SSO) was established in January, 1948. The first subscription concert, conducted by J.S. Kim in February, 1948. After 14 concerts, J.S. Kim was named full-time Music Director, and a support group, the Seoul Symphony Association, was born.

In April of 1950, the SSO acquired instruments and music worth between $40,000 and $50,000 (US) from a former Chief Director of the KSO. All former members of the KSO were also retained. Then the devastating blow struck.

Invasion from the North in June 1950 was a shock felt worldwide. The direct effect on the orchestra was disastrous, as many members were forcibly taken into North Korea and many valuable instruments were destroyed. Once again, the music stopped, but this time the silence was like that following a death knell. Again however, the incredible strength and determination of the Korean people was demonstrated. After an attempt at resurrection of the SSO, it incorporated as the Navy Symphony and Chorus, consisting of capable naval personnel and numbering 105 persons. The inaugural concert in November, 1950, was held at Shi-Gong Hall.

The Navy Symphony and Chorus was renamed the Navy Symphony Orchestra (NSO) and soon increased its membership. The Korean Symphony Association, a new corporation, was set up as a support group, with J.S. Kim as chief Director. In March of 1957, the orchestra made a two-month tour of Hong Kong, Taipei and Saigon, on a goodwill mission. Soon the Seoul Metropolitan Council approved the establishment of an orchestra, and on August 14th of 1957, the Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra (SPO), with its 82 members under the baton of Maestro Kim, was officially founded.

This sensational event was a real turning point for symphonic music in Korea. By 1961, the orchestra had given 90 concerts. In accord with a new municipal ordinance regarding establishment of orchestras, the Second Mayor of the Seoul Metropolitan Area named a General Director; two staffs, one for management and one for performers, were created. J.S. Kim first took the principal Conducting post, then handed the baton over in July of 1961 to Man-Bok Kim.

Tragically, many professional artists had died in action during the Korean War, and this left a dearth of soloists in the fifties and early sixties. A typical subscription concert given during that period showcased a young student, soloing in a concerto with the SPO. Today, most of these same young soloists are well-known, established professionals.

In March of 1965, the orchestra made a successful concert tour of Japan. It was the first international tour for the SPO. Then, in August of 1970, following the resignation of Man-Bok Kim, Kyung-Soo Won assumed his Post as Music Director and Conductor. In 1974, Chai-Dong Chung took the post and remains there today, steering the SPO toward its future.

Maestro Chung's appointment proved to be another turning point for the SPO. The full membership increased to 110 musicians, enabling performances of huge orchestrations by Romantics like Richard Strauss, Mahler and Bruckner. In May 1977, the orchestra went on a successful Asian tour, performing in Taiwan, Hong Kong, Thailand, Malaysia and Singapore. This brought the orchestra into international view.

The orchestra found a permanent home with the opening of the beautiful Seoul Sejong Cultural Center in 1978. The Seoul Metropolitan Government engaged the SPO there in July of that year. Since then the SPO has succeeded in improving both the quality as well as the variety of its concerts. Special projects include Pan-Generation Concerts, which include new music by Korean composers, Christmas Carol concerts, Pops concerts, which are a hit with audiences every year, and concerts for important national Ceremonies and holidays. Subscription concerts these days include guest conductors and soloists alike from the highest international rank. The SPO is now nearing its 380th subscription concert.

In November 1982, the orchestra toured the Western United States, stopping in Los Angeles, Santa Barbara, San Francisco and Honolulu. In May of 1986, the SPO embarked on another American tour to help publicize the Asian Games of that year and the coming Seoul Olympiad. The tour performances, in New York, Washington, D. C., Chicago, San Francisco, and Los Angeles, drew enthusiastic response from critics and packed theaters full of eager audiences.

The Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra continues to gain worldwide recognition for its fine performances, and continues to add new talent to its ranks while fostering the development of young musicians on the domestic scene. Under Maestro Chung's visionary leadership, the orchestra looks forward to an increasing number of international tours while continuing to satisfy musical appetites at home.

강 수 일 (姜秀日)/지휘자
대구시립교향악단의 지휘자인 그는 1964년 경복 중촌에서 태어났다. 그의 최초의 정규적인 음악교육은 서울예고에서 이루어졌으며, 서울대학교 음악대학을 졸업한 후, 미국의 미시간 주립대학교에서 학사 및 석사학위를 받았다. 그는 국립교향악단 (현KBS교향악단)에서 15년간 더불 베이스 주자로 있었으며, 1980-85년에는 미시간주립대학교에서 Dennis Burh의 assistant conductor로 일하였다. 또한 그는 서울예고와 예원중학교의 지휘자로도 있었다. 1985년 이후로 그는 대구시립교향악단과 계명대학교의 교향악단을 지휘해오고있다.

Eun-Seong Park: Born in the year of Korea's liberation, Eun-Seong Park's life reflects the same artistic growth his country has experienced. Mr. Park completed his studies in Violin Performance at Seoul National University's College of Music. After graduating, he joined the National Symphony Orchestra as a first violinist, a post he held until 1974. He has also been a member of the Seoul String Quartet (1972) and the Austria Bruckner Symphony Orchestra (1973). He began his conducting studies at the Salzburg International Summer Academy in 1975, and became the first Korean to graduate from the Department of Conducting at the Hochschule für Musik und Darstellende Kunst in Wien (Vienna School of Music and Performing Arts), where he worked with Othmar Sutner, Music Director of the East Berlin Opera House and Honorary Conductor of the NHK Symphony Orchestra (Tokyo). Eun-Seong Park Has guest-conducted the Vienna Tonkunstler Orchestra and the American Symphony Orchestra. Since returning home in 1981, he has conducted performances by the NSO, SPO, KBS Symphony Orchestras, and at the Korean Music Festival, and all other professional orchestras in the Republic of Korea. In addition to conducting many operas in the standard repertoire, he has premiered many new Korean operas. He currently serves as Music Director and Conductor of Seoul Junior Philharmonic Orchestra, as well as assisting Maestro Chung with the conducting duties of SPO

세미나연사 및 사회자 소개/SPEAKERS

이 상 만(李相萬)은 서울대학교에서 작곡과 미학을 전공한 뒤, 유네스코 장학금을 받아 벨기에에서 Arts in Media를 공부했으며, 예일대학교에서 Theater Administration, 뉴욕대학교에서 Financing and Economics in the Arts, 그리고 UCLA에서 Arts Management를 공부했다. 그는 서라벌대학교와 한양대학교에서 음악사, 음악미학, 그리고 한국전통음악 등을 강의하였다. 그는 「계석」의 주필이며, 한국의 주요 신문에 음악비평을 쓰고 있다. 또한 그는 수많은 연구논문을 발표하였다.
그는 KBS방송국의 음악부의 책임자로 있었으며, 대한민국 음악제를 포함한 여러 음악제의 운영위원으로 일했다. 또한 그는 대통령 포상과 문교부장관 포상을 받은 바 있다.

Sang-Man Lee graduated form Seoul National University after majoring in Composition and Aesthetics. He continued his studies in Arts in Media in Belgium with a UNESCO scholarship, and has also studied Theater Administration at Yale University, Financing and Economics in the Arts at New York University, and Arts Management at UCLA.
Mr. Lee has lectured at Korea University, Sorabul University and Hanyang University in Seoul on Music History, Aesthetics in Music, and Korean Traditional Music. He is the Editor and Executive Director of "Kaeksuk," the most representative music journal in Korea, and has written music reviews for major newspapers in Korea. He is the author of numerous monographs and research papers.
Mr. Lee heads the Music Department of the KBS(Korea Broadcasting System), and has served as Executive Board Member for many festivals in Korea, incuding the Korean Music Festival. He has been the recipient of the Presidential Award and the Minster of Education Award.

박 재 성(朴在成): 서울대학교 음악대학 작곡과와 동대학원 작곡과를 졸업한 (M.A. in Composition) 그는 1983년 渡美하여 1988년 뉴욕주립대학교 (Buffalo)에서 박사학위(Ph. D. in Music Theory)를 취득하였다. 유학시에는 좋은 Graduate Fellowship을 받으며 "Structure and Material of Music"을 강의 했으며, 또한 미국의 3대 주요 음악이론 저널 중의 하나인< Music Theory Spectrum>의 Editor조교로서 중요한 학문적 경험을 하였다. John Clough교수의 지도로 쓰여진 박사학위 논문에서, 그는 無調音樂의 분석방법을 제시하고 있으며, 특히 그의 "RIP개념"은 James Baker로부터 "대단한 잠재력을 지닌 분석수단으로서, 집합이론의 분석분야에 중요한 공헌을 하였으며, 無調音樂의 연구에서 표준이 될 것임을 확신한다"는 평가를 받았다. 이 논문은 1989년 미국 UMI에서 출판되었다.
계명대학교 음악대학 작곡과 교수로 9년간 재직한 후, 현재는 한양대학교 음악대학 작곡과 부교수로 재직 중이며, 음악이론과 작곡을 가르치고 있다.

Jae-Sung Park Born in Korea in 1952, Jae-Sung Park studied at Seoul National University (B.A. and M.A. in Composition) and received his Ph.D. in Music Theory from the State University of New York at Buffalo. He is currently an associate professor of Theory and Composition at Hanyang University. His dissertation, "A Study of Pitch-Class Structure in Anton Webern's Early Atonal Songs (1908-09)," offers some analytical methods for atonal music.
Mr. Park's compositions include: Note I for solo clarinet; Note II for two oboes, two clarinets and one bassoon; "AD EsCHBEG" for violin, cello and piano; and Sound Structure for Orchestra.

=== Page 53 ===
Maya Pritzker: Born and educated in Moscow, is one of the Soviet Union's leading musical critics. She has published more than 200 articles on many musical subjects, and has focussed special attention on the works of Soviet composers. She is a member of the Composers' Union of the USSR, and is editor of the journal Musical Life.

Olga Termini: is a musicologist and Professor of music history. She specializes in vocal music of the 17th and early 18th centuries, particularly Venetian opera and the music of Carlo Francesco Pollaro. Her essays and articles have appeared in such publications as the New Grove's Dictionary of Music and Musicians, the R.M.A. Research Chronicle, and the Music Review. Dr. Termini's current work centers on an archival study of a church in Brescia, Italy. She has written program notes for many concerts and is active in the American Musicological Society. She teaches a wide variety of music history and interdisciplinary courses at California State University, Los Angeles. She is the recipient of the Trustees' Outstanding Professor Award, California State University System, 1989-90.

Kyungsun Suh was born in 1942 in Seoul, Korea. She graduated from Seoul National University's College of Music in 1964, received her M.A. in Composition in 1968, and M.M. in Theory from the University of Massachusetts in 1972. In 1981, she received a grant from the Heinrich-Hertz Stiftung in West Germany to take part in a theatre and video project with Mauricio Kagel at the Cologne Musikhochschule.

Her chamber works have been performed at the annual Composer's Forum of the Contemporary Music Society in Seoul and the Asian Composers League. She has received commissions from music festivals in Seoul, Rome, and Wellington (Asian-Pacific Music Festival, 1984).

Currently Kyung-Sun Suh is Professor of Theory and Composition at the College of Music, Hanyang University. She is also a member of the Korean Committee of ACL, C.M.S. S., and vice-president of the Korean Music Society of Women Composers.

①のソロはすべて長音のみとする。
①〜④の奏法を自由に組み合わせて様々なフレーズを作り出すこと。核音群における音高の下降の長音句は必ず用いること。
最初の音は⑥が望ましい。

収穫部分
全奏者①の奏法のみとする。音高は任意。但し次第に下記の音高に近づける。各奏者がこの音高に近づけたら反復を続けること。

CROSS TALK is a series of events aimed at presenting to Japanese audiences well-prepared performances of works representing current trends in Japanese and American music. On the day preceding each concert, an informal open rehearsal will be held for a small invited audience of young Japanese composers, performers, and critics. Discussion will be encouraged between guests, the performers, and, whenever possible, the composers. Scores will be available and programs have been prepared with the idea of including a wide range of useful information. Musical examples given in the programs suggest the notational procedure of each composer. In order to make available the widest range of information and experience, extra events will occasionally be held. The time and place of these meetings which will feature films, electronic music, chamber and solo performances, will be announced as needed.

* * *

I would like to thank Kuniharu Akiyama, Joji Yuasa, Karen and Roger Reynolds for their efforts in organizing the CROSS TALK series. Design of the poster and program layout and coordination were done by Karen Reynolds; for verbal and written translation, thanks go to Sumio Kambayashi (specifically for the Japanese versions of the Ives and Subotnick notes), Roger Reynolds, Kuniharu Akiyama, Naomichi Kimura, and Gen Iwasaki.

We are particularly grateful for the cooperation of Akeo Watanabe in assembling the performers as well as for his conducting. Finally, appreciation is due Mr. Masuzo Saito of Asahi Shinbun and Mr. Shin Kugimoto of the International Music Society for their assistance.

- Donald Albright, Director
  American Cultural Center, Tokyo

=== Page 15 ===
の発展として、この＜イコン＞を作ったつもりです。

しかし＜イコン＞の場合には、音の方向性を完全に制御することを意図して、音源及び音像の移動が5チャンネルを通して作曲されています。そこでは音を聴く人間が、実際の生活空間に於けるように音に包まれてしまいます。

私はそこに無限に拡がる音の地平線をイメージし、更に故鈴木大拙師がよく宇宙的無意識（Cosmic Unconsciousness）と言っておられましたが、宇宙と人間との一体感といった、或る意味で非常に原初的なイメージを持ったのでした。（湯浅譲二）

この曲は大きくわけて四つの部分からなっていますが、その中で、フォルムと音色という二つの重要なファクターが全く反対の形をとりながら変貌していきます。つまり、形の上からは、ソリッドな固いフォルムをもった音たちが、次第にプラスティックなくずれた形へと変化し解消していきますが、音色の上ではそれとは、逆に疎から密へ移行していく構造を持っています。

section from directional score for Icon by Joji Yuasa; vertical axis = A,B,C,D,E channels; horizontal axis = time

湯浅譲二の電子音楽＜イコン＞の方向性に関する譜面、縦軸は上から A,B,C,D,E の各5チャンネル、横軸は時間を示す。
